result.lens: PRODUCTION SYSTEMS and evaluation: substrate (bus + event-sourced ledger + per-message trace streams + fsync + 18 packages in one process) judged against the actual load (one laptop, one family, ~1.4 GB / 118k stream files after two weeks) and the actual need (one process, resume after crash, auditability, a voice path with a human waiting); tracing, latency budgets, evals as the gate, per-step model routing, and safety tiers.

what_sim_got_right.decision: The action path is structural, not policy: only Guardian subscribes to action.proposed, only Execution to action.approved, approval is an HMAC over (action_id | tool | sha256(args) | expires), Execution re-verifies, and kernel/selfcheck.py proves the wire (forged token refused, pause denies) before any work runs.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Every 2026 harness pattern this review recommends (native tool calling, sub-agents, MCP servers, skills, computer-use) produces MORE ways for a model to reach an effect. A chokepoint enforced by the bus topology survives all of them unchanged: a native tool_use block, an MCP tool and a sub-agent's call all still become one action.proposed. This is the one design decision that lets the rest be swapped freely.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep verbatim. Strengthen by recording every Guardian decision (rule that fired, tier, posture) as a span attribute on the turn, so approvals/denials per tier per day is a dashboard number rather than a ledger grep.

what_sim_got_right.decision: contracts/ is the only shared dependency, enforced by an AST boundary test; kernel/registry.py is the single composition root; the Tool protocol already carries name, description, read_only, reversibility and args_schema (contracts/protocols.py:195-200).
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Native tool calling needs a JSON schema per tool; the safety tiers below need a reversibility class per tool; MCP needs a tool descriptor. All three already exist on the Tool protocol. The migration to structured tool use is a serialization of what is there, not a redesign, and the boundary test keeps any one package replaceable without a rewrite.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep. Strengthen by making args_schema the single source for the model-facing tool definition, the CLI `tool` command, and Guardian's subject extraction (guardian/rules.py _SUBJECT_ARG_KEYS currently guesses 'subject'/'path').

what_sim_got_right.decision: Task state is an append-only task:<id> stream, and orchestration/resume.py distinguishes a crash (continue the same attempt, steps already spent) from a retry (fresh budget, carried notes, kept uncommitted edits).
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: This is exactly the checkpoint-and-resume shape long-horizon agents need. The event stream per task is also the raw material for replayable traces: a task's stream already contains every think, every action and every result, in order.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep as the ONLY event-sourced truth for agent state (task, action, guardian, plan, memory writes, self-model). Strengthen by adding an explicit checkpoint event after every irreversible action and by treating the stream as the replay fixture for evals (see evals package).

what_sim_got_right.decision: Honest floors everywhere: a floor-answered benchmark case is skipped rather than scored wrong; a memory block that could not be consulted says so in the prompt (context.py MEMORY_UNAVAILABLE_NOTE); a suite that cannot be scored to the published scorer is refused (benchmark/README).
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Eval-driven development only works if the numbers are trustworthy. Most teams discover late that outages, floor answers and partial runs contaminated their baseline; Sim already labels them. This discipline is what makes the migration below measurable at each stage.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep. Strengthen by sizing noise explicitly (the 2026-09-15 finding: two identical L3 runs gave 3/21 and 9/25) -- every capability suite reports a confidence interval from >=3 repeats before any switch flips.

what_sim_got_right.decision: Measurement from the ledger and the running system (tools/trial.py, tools/trial_suite.py, observer waves, benchmark unit that drives task.create through the whole bus rather than calling Cognition), plus the retrospective's own conclusion that shape tests missed every blocker.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: This is the seed of an eval harness in the 2026 sense: scripted tasks, automatic pass/fail on system behaviour, repeated until stable. The project already learned the lesson most agent teams learn a year in.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Strengthen into the primary gate: trial_suite + benchmark + a household suite become `simorgh/evals`, and simloader's bless runs them (it already can with --full) rather than CORE_TESTS alone.

what_sim_got_right.decision: simloader.py: stdlib-only bootloader that never runs the code it judges, tags sim-good-N only after an independent gate, bounded rollback, decisions printed and written where Sim reads them.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: A self-editing agent needs an A/B image pattern with an external judge; this is it. It also gives the substrate migration a safe shape: every stage lands behind the same gate and rolls back the same way.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep. Make the gate the eval suite (not only unit tests) and add a 'watch' phase: after handoff, the loader stays alive for N minutes and counts span-level SLO breaches (voice p95, tool error rate) as a bad image.

what_sim_got_right.decision: Cognition's production plumbing: per-provider rolling budgets replayed from the ledger, estimated-cost check before dialling, a shared deadline split across failover candidates, transient retry, cooldown circuit breaker, truncated-retry with doubled tokens, image-capable filtering.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Per-step routing (frontier vs fast vs local) is a policy layered on exactly these primitives: candidate order, budget, deadline share. Nothing here needs replacing.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep. Add the missing input to routing: a latency budget and a risk tier per request, so the router chooses the route rather than only the order.

what_sim_got_right.decision: Every tool has a reversibility class (read_only | reversible | irreversible) and anything unlisted defaults to irreversible (orchestration/tools.py); Guardian's last rule gates on it; Execution's write-watching and worktree landing make code edits revertible commits.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Reversibility-weighted oversight is the accepted way to give an agent autonomy without giving it blast radius. The classes exist; they only need to become explicit tiers with different approval, rate limits and audit.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep; formalise as four tiers (below) and restore the human gate for tier 3 only, which the 2026-09-07 auto-approve default currently collapses.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Tool calls are parsed out of free text by a marker protocol (cognition/parser.py: one string per MARKER: line, _CODE_BEARING_MARKERS and MARKER_SPLIT_FIRST_LINE hacks for multi-arg tools). Every provider adapter accepts tools= and drops it (together.py complete() -> _complete_sync(messages, max_tokens, timeout)); cognition/service.py:358 passes tools=None to the router. session.py then polices the text with seven regex families (invented_markers, unhonoured_marker, _transcript_echo, claimed_to_commit, promised_behaviour, claimed_tv_act, claimed_to_note_a_pronunciation), each a live-caught incident turned into a heuristic.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Native structured tool use: tools sent as JSON schemas, the model returns typed tool_use blocks with ids, results go back as tool_result blocks bound to those ids, several calls per turn are normal. The harness never parses prose for intent; a claim of an action with no tool_use block is simply text.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Reliability and step cost. Each police rule exists because prose and action are the same channel. With typed calls, fabricated-result echo, invented tools, first-line-only arguments and 'promised behaviour' are not failure modes of the protocol; the regexes and their 1,100 dated comments stop being load-bearing. args_schema already exists on every Tool, so this is a serializer plus adapter changes, not a redesign.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Tracing is a Ledger stream per message: trace:<trace_id> files, 88,356 of them, fsync per append, retention by deleting files older than 2 days, boot stats the directory. Metrics (metrics:history 114 MB), curiosity ticks (43 MB) and mood samples (persona:state 17 MB) are appended to the same event log with the same durability as a git commit.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: OpenTelemetry-shaped tracing: one trace per turn/task, spans for think, guardian, tool, verify, stt, tts with start/end, status and attributes; stored in a queryable table (sqlite WAL is enough at this scale); sampled and retained per root span; telemetry (metrics, ticks, mood) in a time-series table with row-level retention and downsampling, never in the decision log.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Latency questions ('why was that turn 9 s?') are unanswerable today without joining 88k files; disk grows ~700 MB/week from streams no decision depends on; the ledger's durability guarantee is paid on every mood sample. A spans table answers p50/p95 per stage in milliseconds and is the substrate every SLO below is measured on.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Default ledger backend is one JSONL file per stream with fsync per append and a snapshot every 200 events; sqlite WAL exists (ledger/backends/sqlite.py) but is not the default. Projections (Planning's TaskStore, Learning's competence, Memory's recall index) rebuild by replaying streams at boot.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Event-sourced only where the events ARE the decisions (task, action, guardian, plan, self-model, memory writes); everything derived lives as relational projections in the same sqlite file, updated incrementally and queryable with SQL; jsonl kept as an export/import format.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: 118k files and 1.4 GB for one household's fortnight; boot cost proportional to file count; 'list open tasks' is a replay, not a query. The sqlite backend already exists; the divergence is defaults and the absence of projection tables.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: A CLI chat turn is a throwaway Session (interface/service.py:943 mints a uuid per typed line); there is no transcript; continuity is three memory recalls (matched, recent-6, per-person) over hashed bag-of-words vectors, scoring every record, under a 0.25 s timeout that is crossed at ~1,000 records under load (context.py's own comment).
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: A durable conversation (thread) per channel and person, with a transcript that is compacted, plus tiered memory: working = the thread; episodic = turns; semantic = distilled facts; procedural = skills. Retrieval is an index lookup over real embeddings (a pre-warmed local embedder, vectors persisted), not a scan under a timer.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: 'What did I just say?' fails by construction; the memory block silently vanishes once the store is the size consolidation itself targets (2,000 per kind). The 24.9 s sentence-transformers cold start is a boot-time warm-up problem, not a reason to use hashing at recall time.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: The voice path has one 95 s reply timeout (voice/config.py reply_timeout_s) and a 20 s TTS stall timeout; cognition chat max_seconds is 90 s; the bus request default is 30 s and the memory-bus handler timeout is 300 s. Measured 2026-09-18: stt 1.8-6.8 s, llm 1.3-9.5 s, full response 4-17 s. No deadline travels with the message; no stage has a budget.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: End-to-end latency budgets: a deadline in the envelope, propagated and shrunk at each hop; per-stage budgets (STT final, first model token, first audio) with breaches recorded as span events; fast-tier routing and streaming for conversational turns so first audio does not wait for the whole reply.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Nothing enforces the budget a person experiences; every timeout is a local guard. Without spans the p95 is not even known per stage, so the 4-17 s spread cannot be attributed.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Routing is an ordered failover list plus one 'strong' tier requested by orchestration on attempt >= N or after a helper returned nothing (session.py _tier; cognition/service.py routes['strong']). A chat turn and a patch step take the same primary route; reasoning_effort is a constant 'low'.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Per-step routing by (purpose, risk tier, context size, latency budget, expected difficulty): a fast/cheap model for tool-argument formatting, summaries, backchannel and simple chat; the frontier model for planning, code changes and verification; local only as fallback; effort/thinking as a routed parameter; route quality measured per suite.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Cost and latency are spent uniformly; the one lever that could halve voice latency (route chat to a fast tier, stream) is not a routing input today.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: 447 test files / 90k lines assert code shape; the 8-minute gate is unit tests; the project's own retrospective (07-post-cutover-review.md section 4) says they missed every real blocker; real bugs came from trial.py, trial_suite.py, observer waves and benchmark waves.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Eval-driven development: capability suites with scripted tasks and automatic scoring; replayable traces (record a task's spans and provider responses, replay with a fixture provider to test the harness deterministically); regression benchmarks per capability with noise sizing; the eval suite is the release gate.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Unit tests remain useful for contracts and pure functions, but the gate measures the wrong thing. The pieces of the right gate already exist in tools/ and benchmark/; they are not a package, not deterministic, and not what bless runs by default.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: The growth layer: Learning is unreachable (no publisher for learn.pipeline.run; proposes draft_candidate which is not registered -- learning/service.py UNREACHABLE), Reflection observes, Curiosity writes a 43 MB tick stream, and the Self Model's capabilities['tools'] is never written.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Skills as procedural memory are the unit of learning: a successful trajectory is distilled into a SKILL.md, evaluated on a held-out variant, promoted or discarded; code self-patches land only through the worktree + eval gate; competence is computed from eval results, not self-reported outcomes.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Learning produces no measured capability change; three packages implement one loop's three halves without the middle (evaluation). use_skill and simorgh_skills already exist, so the promotion loop is the missing piece.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Guardian: 12 rules in fixed order, posture (guarded/trusted/locked), irreversible_requires_human, and since 2026-09-07 sim.sh auto-approves irreversible actions. Reversibility is binary at the last rule.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Explicit safety tiers tied to reversibility, blast radius and origin, each with its own approval, rate limit and audit; the human gate reserved for the tier where it is cheap and matters (external, physical, financial); tightening automatic, loosening human-only.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: With auto-approve on, a git commit in a worktree and a siren or a message to a third party are the same tier. Tiering restores the human gate exactly where the creator would want to be asked, without slowing the rest.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: One asyncio process runs 18 packages; heavy work (whisper, TTS engines, ffmpeg HLS, pytest -n auto for landing) runs in threads or subprocesses inside it; a busy tool thread ignored SIGTERM until os._exit was added; a 300 s bus handler timeout was every task's wall budget until made unbounded.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: A single-loop harness with sub-agents in isolated contexts, and heavy or latency-critical services (STT/TTS, sandboxes, test runs) out of process behind deadlines and health, so a stuck engine cannot stall the loop or block shutdown.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: local-multi mode already exists for workers; voice engines and the landing gate are the two things that still hold the main loop hostage.

target_architecture.one_paragraph: Keep the bus, the contracts-only import rule, the Guardian chokepoint and the kernel; change what is underneath and around them. The Ledger becomes a sqlite-WAL store by default with two halves: a decision log that stays event-sourced (task:<id>, action:<id>, guardian, plan, memory writes, self-model changes) and a telemetry store of plain tables (spans, metrics_ts, samples) with row-level retention; jsonl becomes export/import. Tracing becomes spans: one root span per turn or task, child spans per think, guardian decision, tool call, verify, stt and tts, written by the bus trace writer into the spans table and sampled per root. Tool calling becomes native: a ToolSchema serialised from each Tool's args_schema is sent to providers that support it, the model's tool_use blocks become action.proposed unchanged, results return as tool_result messages, and the marker protocol survives only as a fallback for Ollama and the floor. Orchestration gains a durable Conversation (thread per channel and person, transcript, compaction) so a typed line is a turn in a thread rather than a session; Memory gains a persisted vector index over a pre-warmed real embedder. A deadline field in the envelope propagates end to end and a per-step router picks a route by purpose, risk tier, context size and latency budget. Learning, Reflection and Curiosity merge into one Growth package whose unit of learning is a skill promoted by evaluation; benchmark, trial.py, trial_suite.py and observer_kit merge into an Evals package that is the loader's bless gate. Safety tiers are explicit on every action and every Guardian decision is a span attribute.

modules.from: keep (simorgh/ledger), default backend switched to sqlite
modules.responsibility: Decision log (event-sourced, per-stream seq, CAS) plus projection tables and a blob store, in one WAL database; jsonl as export/import.
key_algorithms_or_methods: sqlite WAL with (stream, seq) primary key for CAS (already in backends/sqlite.py)
projection tables updated incrementally on append (tasks, actions, competence) instead of replay-at-boot; replay kept as the rebuild path
row-level retention per table (DELETE WHERE ts < cutoff) replacing per-file deletion
group_commit: batch fsync for telemetry writes, per-append fsync only for decision streams
modules.interfaces: Unchanged Ledger protocol (append/read/head/snapshot/blobs) for decision streams; new `query(table, where)` for projections; `export_jsonl(stream)` / `import_jsonl`.

modules.name: telemetry
modules.from: merge of bus/trace.py + kernel/metrics.py + the read side of interface/dashfeeds
modules.responsibility: Spans, metrics and samples: every turn/task is a trace with child spans; metrics and mood/tick samples go to time-series tables; SLO evaluation per stage.
key_algorithms_or_methods: OpenTelemetry-shaped span model: trace_id, span_id, parent_id, name, start, end, status, attrs(JSON); the existing trace_id/causation_id on Message map directly
sampling per root span (keep every span of a sampled turn), not per message
downsampling of metrics_ts on the sleep tick (1 s -> 1 min after a day)
SLO table: stage -> budget; breach = span event, counted per day
modules.interfaces: `span(name, parent, attrs)` context manager offered via Context to every subsystem; `spans.query(trace_id)`; `simorgh trace <id>` renders the tree from the table; HTTP /api/traces and /api/metrics read it.

modules.name: cognition
modules.from: keep (simorgh/cognition); add toolcalling.py, routing.py; parser.py demoted to fallback
modules.responsibility: Providers with native tool use, per-step routing, budgets, compaction.
key_algorithms_or_methods: ToolSchema serialiser: Tool.args_schema -> provider tool definitions (OpenAI-style function schema for Together/Ollama, Anthropic tool blocks for the Claude path, Gemini function declarations)
tool_use/tool_result message shapes in contracts; a ParsedOutput that carries typed calls with ids
routing table keyed by (purpose, tier, context_tokens_bucket, latency_budget_bucket) -> ordered candidates + effort; measured route quality from evals feeds the table
existing deadline share, cooldown, budget estimate unchanged; deadline now taken from the envelope
modules.interfaces: cognition.think gains `tools: [ToolSchema]`, `deadline`, `risk_tier`; reply carries `tool_calls: [{id, tool, args}]` typed; marker parsing only when the provider lacks tool support.

modules.name: orchestration (harness)
modules.from: keep (simorgh/orchestration); session.py shrinks as the police leave; add conversation.py
modules.responsibility: The single loop: gather -> think -> propose -> verify; durable threads; checkpoints; sub-agent delegation.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Conversation: thread_id = (channel, person); transcript persisted in the decision log; compaction via cognition layers 1-5 on the transcript
tool results returned as tool_result messages bound to tool_use ids; several read-only calls per turn without the _read_batch heuristic
budgets in (tokens, usd, wall) per attempt instead of steps; checkpoint event after every irreversible action; resume.py unchanged in intent
delegate: sub-agent with fresh context and its own budget, returns a summary only (exists; put into an eval arm)
modules.interfaces: percept.text.received carries thread_id; turn.completed carries the thread's compacted state ref; task.step gains span_id.

modules.name: memory
modules.from: keep (simorgh/memory); add index.py; embedders pre-warmed
modules.responsibility: Tiered memory: working (the thread), episodic, semantic, procedural (skills); retrieval by index.
key_algorithms_or_methods: real embedder loaded in a thread at boot (the 24.9 s is paid once, off the critical path); hashing only until it is warm
persisted vector index in sqlite (vectors as blobs, brute-force cosine over an in-RAM float32 matrix is sufficient at 10^4-10^5 records; an ANN library is optional later)
hybrid retrieval: BM25/inverted index + vector, reciprocal-rank fusion, then the existing confidence x recency scoring
consolidation on sleep: episodic -> semantic facts with supersedes links so a correction retires the fact it corrects
modules.interfaces: memory.retrieve unchanged on the wire; adds `thread_id`; the 0.25 s timeout becomes a budget from the envelope deadline.

modules.name: guardian
modules.from: keep (simorgh/guardian); add tiers.py
modules.responsibility: Sole approver; explicit safety tiers; every decision a span attribute.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Tier 0 read-only in scope: allow, log. Tier 1 reversible in scope (worktree edits, memory store, config that can be undone): allow in guarded, deny in locked. Tier 2 irreversible but local and bounded (commit/land, sandboxed shell/script/container, package install, device actions with undo): allow if the tool declares an undo or posture is trusted, else escalate; rate-limited per hour. Tier 3 external, physical or financial (notify a third party, run_remote, sirens, mail send, purchases, publishing): human always, in every posture
tier = f(reversibility, scope, origin, blast_radius) computed from the Tool protocol fields plus a per-tool override table
posture tightening on failure streaks and denial rates (exists); loosening only via human config
modules.interfaces: action.approved/denied gain `tier` and `rule`; guardian.posture unchanged; ui.prompt only for tier 3.

modules.name: execution
modules.from: keep (simorgh/execution); heavy tools moved behind out-of-process services
modules.responsibility: Tools, sandboxes, worktrees, MCP client; structured results.
key_algorithms_or_methods: ToolResult carries a structured payload + blob ref + a short model-facing summary (progressive disclosure replaces the 8,000-char cut)
per-tool deadline from the envelope; a tool call is a span with success/latency
MCP stdio client kept as the integration standard for external services (Home Assistant and similar via their MCP servers, human-configured)
sandbox/test runs and media pipelines as subprocesses with kill-on-deadline, never threads
modules.interfaces: action.result gains `span_id`, `summary`, `result_ref`; tool.registered publishes the ToolSchema list so World Model can finally write capabilities['tools'].

modules.name: verification
modules.from: keep (simorgh/verification)
modules.responsibility: The critic: mechanical checks cheapest-first, checklist, trajectory; also the scorer inside evals.
key_algorithms_or_methods: critic loop only where an oracle exists (tests, schema, diff applies); the LLM reviewer stays off for research (their own finding: not a net gain)
trajectory metrics computed from spans rather than re-reading task streams
modules.interfaces: Unchanged verify.requested/result; a pure-function `score(trajectory, oracle)` exported for evals.

capability_programs.current_state: One think per step; one action per step except read-only batches; tool intent parsed from prose; 'strong' tier only on retry; reasoning_effort fixed at low; the LLM answer reviewer was measured as not a net gain (111 correct and 111 wrong rejected); leading benchmark failure is 'step budget exhausted', not wrong reasoning.
capability_programs.method: Native tool use with several tool_use blocks per turn; effort/thinking as a routed parameter per step (planning and code steps get the frontier route and higher effort, formatting and summaries get the fast route); plan-then-act for tasks whose budget exceeds a threshold, with the plan stored as an artifact in the task stream and re-grounded against it; critic loop only where a mechanical oracle exists (tests, schema, diff applies), never a free-form LLM reviewer on research.

result.agi_honesty: This architecture is a harness around a frontier model: reasoning comes from the provider, and the harness adds memory, tools, safety, continuity and measured improvement. Its ceiling on general capability is the model's ceiling; nothing here learns at the weight level, and the blueprint says so. What the harness CAN deliver, and what 'more general' concretely means for a household agent, is breadth times depth times autonomy: more task domains completed end to end (code, research, home devices, media, calendar, conversation), longer horizons per task (hours, with resume), across more surfaces (voice, chat, TV, phone), with fewer hand-written per-incident heuristics and with a person asked only at tier 3. Progress toward that is measurable as a capability-suite matrix, which is the honest version of the blueprint's 'generality as a queryable number'. The investments that compound are the ones that survive a model swap: eval suites, span data (replayable), skills, the memory index, tool schemas and the safety tiers. The ones that do not compound are regex police, dated incident comments and per-tool argument hacks; they are paid again with every new model. With the migration above, Sim can become a state-of-the-art personal agent harness of the shape production harnesses have in 2026, continuously improving on measured suites. It will not be AGI under any definition that requires learning beyond its model, open-ended competence growth without a human choosing what to measure, or capability that exceeds the frontier model it routes to; calling it that would contradict the SOUL.md directive on transparency.
result.biggest_risk_of_this_proposal: Half-migration. The project's own dominant bug shape is the unconnected wire (a slot with one side implemented), and a substrate migration is the largest producer of unconnected wires there is: two trace formats, two tool protocols, two memory indexes, two budgets, each half-read by something. For one developer working through coding agents, the failure mode is a live, self-editing system that boots from a checkout with both halves present, where the loader's gate is green because the unit suite still asserts the old shape. Mitigation is ordering and deletion discipline: telemetry first (stage 0) because every later stage is judged by it; evals as the gate (stage 3) before routing or long-horizon changes; every stage behind a config switch; and no stage begins until the previous stage's old path has been deleted and the eval suite has passed on the deleted-path build. The Guardian invariant and corrigibility are untouched by every stage, which is what makes the migration safe to do live.

result.lens: Cognitive architecture and long-horizon autonomy: memory tiers and retrieval, self model and world model as estimated quantities, goal trees with checkpoints and critics for multi-day work, and a growth loop that actually closes (outcome -> estimate -> proposed change -> evaluated -> adopted -> retired). Verified against the code at /Users/saeed/ws/Simorgh on 2026-09-18; no files modified, nothing booted, no paid calls.

what_sim_got_right.decision: All state is an append-only Ledger of events and every status, competence figure and the Self Model are (meant to be) projections rebuilt from the log (ledger/, learning/competence.py::CompetenceTable is a real fold over learn:outcomes; orchestration/resume.py rebuilds attempts from task:<id>).
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Long-horizon agents live or die on checkpoint/resume and on replayable history. Every pattern this proposal needs -- durable goal trees, checkpoints, a fact store with supersession, competence posteriors, eval baselines -- is 'one more projection over streams that already exist'. Nothing has to be re-platformed.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Strengthen: make the Self Model and the memory indexes actual projections with snapshots (today the Self Model is in-memory only and the recall index is rebuilt at boot). Add a `checkpoint` event type to task streams. Keep fsync-per-append for action/task streams; move high-volume trace/metrics streams to batched appends (that is a ledger lens problem, but it is what makes the cognitive projections cheap).

what_sim_got_right.decision: Structural safety: proposal -> Guardian (12 rules, HMAC) -> Execution, enforced by bus topology and proved at boot, with corrigibility (pause/stop) as the first rule.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Every serious 2026 agent harness is bolting a permission chokepoint on after the fact; Sim has it natively, which is exactly what lets a self-improving loop be safe: a learned policy, a new skill, a routing change or a self-patch can all be 'just another proposal'. The growth loop below adopts nothing except through action.proposed.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep unchanged. Strengthen by giving the growth loop's policy store (`growth:policies`) protected-subject status for loosening and by adding one Guardian rule: a proposal may add guidance or restrictions to a task type's rules, never touch guardian/, contracts/, kernel/, execution/verifier.py (already protected) or the policy store's own gate.

what_sim_got_right.decision: Worker/Session separation with lease heartbeat, attempts that carry a note, and resume from the task's own stream (orchestration/worker.py, resume.py, session.py::_run).
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: This is the skeleton of a checkpoint-and-resume long-horizon agent: a task already survives crashes and spans attempts. What is missing is a model-authored checkpoint (the progress note exists but is off) and explicit waiting states, not a new loop.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Strengthen: turn on `reground_every_steps=3` (the spec's own value, 16-orchestration.md 3.5); persist the model's progress note as the carried note between attempts instead of the mechanical 220-char-per-step summary; add WAITING(until|event|human) as a task status with scheduler wake-ups.

what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: A self model that is an estimated quantity with uncertainty, not a string, is what makes directed exploration (Thompson sampling over Beta posteriors), model escalation and honest 'I am bad at X' possible. The primitive is right; it is under-consumed (compute_gaps returns [], strategy.suggest has no caller).

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Paraphrases score 0.0 (measured in embedders.py); a correction and the thing it corrected arrive as peers; 'the machine names' failure documented in context.py is structural, not a tuning problem. target_architecture.one_paragraph: Keep the substrate (Bus, Ledger, Kernel), the action path (Guardian, Execution, Verification) and Cognition's routing seam exactly as they are. Rebuild the cognitive core behind unchanged contracts: Memory becomes four real tiers with a fact store and hybrid retrieval; World Model becomes two durable projections -- a Self Model of estimated quantities and an Environment State of household entities -- and absorbs Persona's user model; Planning becomes goal trees with acceptance criteria, checkpoints, waiting states and a checkpoint critic; Orchestration keeps its one loop but runs persistent threads, progress-note compaction and isolated delegation. Merge Learning, Reflection and Curiosity into one Growth subsystem that owns a single loop over a versioned policy store: estimate (posteriors), diagnose (failure clusters), propose (rule | skill | routing | patch), evaluate (held-out cases in a worktree), adopt (through Guardian), retire (TTL and regression). Every recommendation is a projection, a wire, or a merge; none is a rewrite, and nothing acts on the world except through action.proposed.

modules.name: memory
modules.from: keep (internals rebuilt: store.py, recall.py, consolidation.py, embedders.py)
modules.responsibility: Four tiers. Working: not a Ledger stream -- the per-(person, channel) rolling thread (the existing unfed WorkingMemory class, fed from turn.completed keyed by person+channel) plus the current task's progress note. Episodic: turn/step/critique records as today, indexed at write time. Semantic: a fact store `memory:facts` of (subject, predicate, object, valid_from, valid_to, superseded_by, confidence, source_refs, person_scope) with first-class supersession. Procedural: skills (SKILL.md) and adopted growth policies, plus tool-usage recipes distilled from successful trajectories.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Hybrid retrieval: BM25 over real tokens (extend the existing inverted index in recall.py with tf and doc length; stdlib) UNION dense top-N (local sentence-transformers as the optional adapter that already exists in embedders.py), fused by reciprocal rank fusion, then person/time/channel filters and the existing recency and confidence terms. Hashing stays as the floor when the dense index is cold.

Embed at store time in a background thread and persist vectors as a projection file keyed by ref (array('f') per record); warm at boot in the background; recall never waits on embedding. This removes the 24.9 s first-call problem that got the local embedder switched off.

Fact extraction at consolidation: cognition purpose=consolidate returns JSON triples, each with the quoted span it came from; the existing untraceable() check is applied per triple (a triple whose subject/object never appears in the window is dropped). Same-(subject, predicate, scope) with a different object stated by the fact's owner supersedes: append `superseded` and set valid_to on the old fact. Replaces the symmetric 0.5 penalty of flag_contradictions, which currently punishes the correction as much as the error.

Entity linking at recall: names of known people/devices/places in the query (from World Model's entity list) pull their current facts into a separate, small 'facts' block rendered before the episodic block.

Person digest: at sleep, a ~150-token per-person summary regenerated from current facts (never from prose), delivered as a protected block when that person is the speaker; supersedes the regex user_profile facet.
Forgetting: retention score = f(recency, access count, number of linked facts, tombstones); prune episodic below the score, never facts with live links; keep the forget_window tool.
Recall budget raised to ~1.0 s and prefetched: Orchestration issues the recall on percept.text.received (for voice, on the STT partial) in parallel with session setup, so the model waits on nothing.
modules.interfaces: Unchanged topics memory.store/retrieve/forget/stored/consolidated; add memory.fact.stored/superseded and a `facts` field on memory.retrieve.reply; the `working` kind is served from the thread keyed by (person, channel) as well as session_id.

modules.name: worldmodel
modules.from: keep + merge of persona.user_model into it; selfmodel.py becomes a fold of a durable self:model stream
modules.responsibility: Two durable projections. Self Model: state (identity/SOUL hash, registered tools -- written from tool.registered, which is the missing wire -- providers, active goals, restarts) and estimated quantities (competence Beta posteriors per task_type and per (task_type, strategy) with time decay; calibration as expected calibration error; per-tool p(ok) and latency quantiles from action.result; per-provider quality per purpose from verify.result; expected cost per task type; staleness per fact). Environment State: entities (people, rooms, devices, cameras, calendars, vehicles) with observed value, last_seen, source, confidence and typical change rate; fed from action.result of home/media/pim tools, camera.event, tv.state, voice speaker identification, and calendar reads.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Beta(alpha, beta) per task_type with exponential forgetting (weight = 0.5^(age/half_life)); compute_gaps returns areas ranked by posterior mean minus a confidence term, with sample counts -- today it returns [] and Curiosity sees 0.6 everywhere.

Staleness = age / typical change rate learned per entity from its observation history; a 'world now' block renders only entities under a staleness threshold and marks the rest as unknown, so the model never reasons on a device state from yesterday as if current.
Self summary rendered from the posteriors with sample counts ('patch:memory 62% over 13, overconfident'), and a 'what I am bad at' line computed, not copied from limitation strings.
self:model and world:home as Ledger projections with snapshots every N events; rebuilt on boot in milliseconds.
modules.interfaces: Keep self.summary/self.gaps/world.env.query; add world.entity.observed (published) and self.estimate.request/reply (a posterior for a task_type, for Planning risk and Cognition tier choice); PERSONA_USER_MODEL_UPDATED becomes a memory.fact.stored with subject=person.

modules.name: planning
modules.from: keep; model.py, decomposer.py, reground.py, service.py extended
modules.responsibility: Goal trees for any kind of work, not only code: Goal -> Milestone -> Task, each node with acceptance criteria (a checklist Verification can evaluate), a checkpoint ref, a risk estimate from the Self Model, and a waiting_on condition. Owns re-planning: given the tree and what changed since the last checkpoint, revise the subtree and log plan.revised.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Decomposition prompt produces typed nodes {kind: patch|research|action|question|wait, acceptance: [...], depends_on} with kind 'action' scoped to tool families (home, pim, web, files) so a household goal decomposes without naming a repo path.

WAITING status with wake condition (until: ts | event: topic+filter | human: question_id); the Kernel scheduler publishes task.wake; a human answer arrives as a task.answer event and resumes; project sessions wait on children by subscribing to task.completed/failed, never through the work queue (avoids the documented workers=1 deadlock).

Checkpoint critic: at every progress note, Verification's trajectory scorer is asked, against the node's acceptance criteria, for {on_track|drifting|blocked, unmet: [...], next}; two consecutive drifting verdicts trigger re-planning rather than continuing.

Re-grounding as re-planning: replace STILL_VALID yes/no with a structured revision call on the cheap tier that returns the revised subtree; verdict voting (3 cheap samples, majority) for the yes/no cases that remain.

Risk from the Self Model: a node whose task_type posterior mean is below threshold or sample count is low is scheduled with plan mode and a human gate; high-competence nodes run autonomously (reversibility-weighted oversight, principle 4.10, now data-driven).
modules.interfaces: Keep plan.proposed/approved/revised, task.*; add task.waiting, task.wake, task.answer, plan.node.verified. Rollup stays a pure function of children.

modules.name: orchestration
modules.from: keep; switch on what exists, add threads and checkpoint hooks
modules.responsibility: One loop, unchanged shape: gather -> think -> act (through Guardian) -> verify. Runs persistent conversation threads, progress-note compaction, isolated delegation, and publishes checkpoints the critic and resume can use.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Progress-note re-grounding on (reground_every_steps=3, keep_recent_steps=2); the note becomes the carried note across attempts and the checkpoint the critic scores.
Persistent thread per (person, channel): last N turns kept in Orchestration's WorkingMemory, placed before the memory block; compaction of the thread by the same progress-note mechanism when long.
Delegation on: fresh-context sub-session for research with summary-only return (exists behind `delegation`); parallel read-only batches on.
Escalation: attempt >= 2 or a failed critic verdict routes the next think to the strong tier (escalate_from_attempt=1, `_tier` exists).
Speculative recall: memory and world-now blocks fetched on percept, not on think.
modules.interfaces: Unchanged; task.progress already exists and becomes the checkpoint event; add task.checkpoint.scored consumed from Verification.

modules.name: growth
modules.from: merge of learning + reflection + curiosity (topics preserved; packages folded into simorgh/growth/ with estimate.py, diagnose.py, policies.py, explore.py, monitors.py)
modules.responsibility: The single closed loop over a versioned policy store `growth:policies`. Estimate: outcomes -> posteriors (CompetenceTable, calibration, reliability). Diagnose: at sleep, cluster failures by (task_type, verify failure kind, denied tool, drift kind, critic 'unmet' items) into lesson candidates with evidence refs. Propose: one of four typed artifacts -- a task-type rule (a line rendered by scaffolds for that task_type), a skill, a routing change (purpose or task_type -> tier), or a code patch (through the existing worktree landing). Evaluate: run the candidate against a held-out case set for that task_type (trial suite cases and benchmark cases tagged by task_type) in a worktree; adopt only on no regression plus at least one motivating case fixed. Adopt: through action.proposed(tool=policy_adopt) so Guardian gates it; the policy becomes active and is read by scaffolds.render, the Router and the skills catalog. Retire: TTL and re-evaluation; a policy whose task_type posterior falls after adoption is reverted (bounded rollback, same shape as simloader). Explore: Thompson sampling over competence posteriors and over world-model unknowns chooses idle work.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Thompson sampling: per area draw from Beta(alpha, beta), pick the lowest draw (largest expected gain), then the existing 'ask the model to propose within this target' step; boredom still flattens by raising the temperature. Replaces the constant-gap softmax.

Failure clustering: group terminal failures in the window by a small feature vector (task_type, verify check that failed, tool denied, critic unmet item text hashed); a cluster with >= 3 members and rate above the type's baseline becomes a lesson candidate. Deterministic, no model call; the model is asked only to phrase the rule.

Sequential adoption test: for cheap policies (rules, routing) the eval is the held-out set; for skills and patches it is the full gate plus the held-out set; a candidate never becomes active on its motivating case alone.

Policy artifact schema: {id, kind, task_type|purpose, body, evidence_refs, evaluated_on, baseline, result, adopted_at, ttl, status}. Task-type rules are the first kind because they close the loop with the least machinery: Reflection's lesson becomes a line every future session of that type reads.
Exploration targets extended beyond repo areas: unanswered recurring questions from threads, stale high-query facts, devices never probed, skills never exercised.
modules.interfaces: Keeps publishing learn.*, reflect.*, curiosity.* so no consumer changes; adds growth.policy.proposed/adopted/retired and growth.lesson.found; consumes task.*, verify.result, action.result/denied, plan.node.verified, system.tick.sleep/idle, self.estimate.reply.

result.agi_honesty: What this architecture is: a harness around a cloud model. Its reasoning ceiling is the provider's; Sim does not learn at the weight level and the blueprint rightly says so (01-vision section 3). What it can become, and what compounds: (1) a memory that gets better with every conversation -- facts with supersession, per-person digests, hybrid recall -- so the family experiences an assistant that knows them; (2) a world model of the house so answers come from state and actions are diffs, not re-observation; (3) long-horizon autonomy -- goal trees that pause, wake, re-plan and finish over days without a human holding the thread; (4) procedural learning -- skills, task-type rules and routing that are adopted only when they beat a baseline and retired when they stop helping; (5) calibrated self-knowledge -- posteriors with sample counts driving when to ask, when to escalate and when to act alone. Together these give 'more general' a concrete meaning for a household agent: more task types with measured competence above threshold without per-task engineering, more of the family's world modelled, longer autonomous horizons with fewer interventions, and no safety regressions -- each a number in the ledger, as the blueprint's own AGI stance asks. What it cannot deliver: general intelligence independent of the provider, open-ended learning of new cognitive abilities, or anything that would justify the word AGI in its usual sense; a strong foundation model plus this harness will look far more capable than the same harness on a weak one, and that gap is the model's, not Sim's. Investments that compound: the ledger and evals (every change measured), the fact store (every conversation improves the next), the world model (every observation saves a tool call), skills and policies (every solved problem reusable), and the safety chokepoint (every new capability inherits the gate). Investments that do not compound: per-incident regex heuristics, more tools without persistent state, more prompt text without a policy store, and a bigger test suite that asserts shape. Honest framing for the creator: build toward 'the most capable, trustworthy, self-improving personal agent on one laptop', measured by its own competence table; if the underlying models keep improving, the harness proposed here is the one that will let Sim absorb that improvement without a rewrite.
result.biggest_risk_of_this_proposal: Closing the growth loop before the evaluation harness that must gate it. A self-modifying loop with weak evals will adopt rules, routes and skills that fit their motivating case and quietly regress everything else, and the project's own retrospective (07-post-cutover-review.md section 4) already shows that shape-asserting tests miss exactly this; the trial suite and observer waves are the only things that have ever caught a real blocker. So the order matters more than the content: stage 1's continuity, resume-after-kill and per-task-type case sets are not optional prerequisites, they are the loop's safety mechanism, and no policy kind should be adoptable until its task_type has a held-out set with a stored baseline. The secondary risk is scope drift into a rewrite: the memory rebuild and the growth merge must stay behind unchanged contracts (same topics, same schemas) so the 447-file suite, the boot self-check and the Guardian invariant continue to hold at every commit; the moment a stage requires touching contracts/ and guardian/ together, it has left the proportional path.
