what_sim_got_right.decision: One bus-enforced action path: action.proposed -> Guardian (only subscriber) -> HMAC-bound action.approved -> Execution (only subscriber, re-verifies). Every camera siren, light, cast and door call already goes through it (execution/home/cameras.py docstring: 'Every call is a tool call, so Guardian sees it -- the siren above all').
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: A home agent's failure mode is not a bad answer, it is a bad actuation at 3am. The chokepoint is the one thing that lets presence-aware, person-aware and time-aware rules be added in a single place without any reasoning path being able to route around them. It is also what makes a future 'Home Assistant creates the automation, Sim only proposes it' split enforceable.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep verbatim. Strengthen by carrying the requesting person and channel on every proposal (today Proposal has no requester field; guardian/api.py) so rules can be per person, and by making Guardian recompute physical safety itself (see divergences).

what_sim_got_right.decision: 'Sim does not speak to devices. Sim speaks to Home Assistant.' and 'hard safety automations live in HA, not Sim' (docs/plans/home-automation-design.md section 0), with a pure classify_call in contracts/home/policy.py that is pessimistic by default (unknown domain => human).
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: This is the well-established shape for household agents: one device hub with a uniform entity model (entity_id, state, attributes, domain.service), a local rules engine that survives the agent being down, and an agent that owns judgment rather than drivers. Every serious home-agent stack in 2026 sits on HA or an equivalent hub, not on per-vendor code.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep the decision; actually execute it. HA is not configured today and the designed simorgh/home/ subsystem (bridge, trigger engine, monitors, HomeRule) was never built; only the five home_* tools exist. Section 2.4 (HA events -> percepts) and section 7 (Guardian HomeRule) are the two halves to land first.

what_sim_got_right.decision: Honesty rules in the physical layer: 'ambiguity is refused, never guessed' (execution/home/registry.py), 'report what the house did, not what HA accepted' (home_call snapshots before/after), 'unknown is a real answer' with scores travelling on every identification (voice/speakers.py), and may_refine never learning a voice from a shared or guessed turn.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Trust in a household agent is lost by one confident wrong act: naming the wrong child, turning on the wrong light and saying it was the right one. These rules are the asymmetry a home agent needs: silence and 'I am not sure' are cheap, a wrong actuation is not.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep and generalise into a single contract for perception claims: every percept (speaker, presence, camera description, entity state) carries a confidence and a source, and the prompt renders the confidence rather than the bare claim.

what_sim_got_right.decision: Turn taking as a pure state machine (voice/turns.py: idle/listening/user_speaking/thinking/agent_speaking/interrupted; hybrid end-of-turn with semantic shortening; monotonic turn and response ids so stale audio is dropped) and barge-in gated by an echo tracker fed from what was actually played.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Full-duplex, interruptible conversation is the floor for a voice agent in 2026 and the state machine is exactly the piece that must stay testable without a microphone as latency work (streaming STT, sentence-chunked TTS) lands around it.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep. Strengthen by making the manager consume streaming partials and a streaming reply (so 'agent_speaking' can begin at the first sentence while the model is still generating) and by adding an explicit HOLD state for a proactive utterance waiting for the floor.

what_sim_got_right.decision: Household roster and places in contracts (contracts/household.py with names, sexes, ages, IPA; contracts/places.py house name and network->place map; contracts/overheard.py 48-hour store with purge), so the write side (tools) and the read side (prompt) share one source without importing each other.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: The home agent's most valuable state is small, durable, per-person and per-place. Putting it in contracts is the right instinct for an entity model that every channel and subsystem must agree on.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Strengthen into a real people/entity model (person_id with per-channel identities, role tier, per-person permissions and memory namespace) instead of a frozen tuple plus a voice book plus a Telegram allow-list.

what_sim_got_right.decision: Per-person memory tags (memory/service.py tags person:<name> on voice turns; orchestration/context.py third recall filtered by person and _theirs() so a child's lines are not shown to a stranger) and scaffolds.who_is_here rendering who is speaking, who spoke before, and the room's asides as 'context, not questions'.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Multi-person households need memory partitioning and addressee awareness; most agent frameworks assume one user. Sim already has the seeds of both.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep; extend the person tag to every channel (Telegram/WhatsApp/CLI turns carry no person today) and move the addressee decision out of regexes into a structured percept field.

what_sim_got_right.decision: Measuring from the Ledger (voice:turns carries stt/llm/first_audio/response per turn; docs/module-map.md section 8) rather than from unit tests; durable reminders in kernel/scheduler.py rebuilt from the schedule stream.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Latency, addressee accuracy, presence accuracy and false-announcement rate are the handles that decide whether a family keeps using a voice agent. They are only measurable if every turn is recorded with its timings and outcome, which is already true.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep; add labelled ground truth (who was actually speaking, was it addressed to Sim, who was home) as a small ledger stream the family can correct from the phone, so the handles become precision/recall rather than counts.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: There is no perception subsystem. Percept topics are text/file/web/time only (contracts/topics.py PERCEPT_*). Camera events (world.camera.event) are published by Execution's own camera and Ring watchers and consumed by execution/vision.py, which calls Cognition with images and then speaks via voice.speak.request, all inside Execution. The HA event bridge (design section 2.4) does not exist; HA is not configured.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Embodied agents have a perception layer that turns sensors into typed, timestamped, confidence-bearing percepts (speech with speaker and room, entity state changes, presence evidence, detections with descriptions) that a world model folds and the policy layer consumes. Actuation and perception are separate subsystems.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Execution is both hands and eyes; nothing can subscribe to 'someone arrived at the front door' as a percept, only to a camera channel number. The intelligent layer the design reserved for Sim ('lights on when motion unless it is 3am and someone just went to bed') cannot be written because the 'someone just went to bed' fact exists nowhere.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: There is no world state of the home. The only 'room' is a 16-line deque in voice/session.py (self._room), per voice session, lost on restart. World Model facets are codebase-shaped (file_index, git_state, capability_map, tools, user_profile). Presence is not modelled at all; contracts/places.py stores a house name and a network->place map that is TOLD, not detected.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: A home world state: HA's area/device/entity registry mirrored locally, live entity states via the HA websocket, a presence belief per person per area fused from evidence (speaker id, device trackers, motion, camera person detections) with decay, and derived situation facts (nobody home, quiet hours, TV playing, a child alone). Rendered as a compact block in every prompt and queryable by rules.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: The model reasons about the house from the last 16 spoken lines. Proactive behaviour, routine learning and person-aware safety all need this state and none of them can be built without it.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Identity is per channel and never joined: voice -> SpeakerBook name; Telegram -> allow-list by username, then a session per chat_id (interface/telegram.py); WhatsApp similar; CLI -> implicitly the creator; HA person entities unused. action.proposed carries no requester (guardian/api.py Proposal has no person field), so Guardian cannot know whether a 9-year-old or the owner asked for the siren. Persona's user model extracts two regex facets ('I prefer', 'call me') and is one model, not one per person.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: A person/entity model: one person_id with linked identities (voice embedding set, Telegram id, WhatsApp number, HA person, CLI), a role tier (owner, adult, child, guest, unknown), per-person permissions on tool groups, a per-person memory namespace and a per-person preference model updated from what they actually do, not only from what they say.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Per-person permissions and step-up verification for dangerous requests are impossible today; per-person memory only works for voice; the same family member is three different strangers across channels.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Guardian trusts the proposer's physical safety label. orchestration/tools.py line 700 computes reversibility from classify_call and the comment says 'Guardian recomputes the same answer from the same pure function rather than trusting this', but nothing under simorgh/guardian/ imports classify_call (grep confirms). ReversibilityRule only reads proposal.reversibility. One knob (SIMORGH_GUARDIAN_AUTO_APPROVE, on by default since 2026-09-07) auto-approves irreversible actions for code and for the house alike; policy.py's own docstring says 'for the house that default is wrong'.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Physical actions are gated on a separate axis from code changes: reversibility recomputed at the gate from the arguments, plus who asked, who is present, what time it is, what the alarm state is, per-entity rate limits and safe ranges, with hard safety living in HA. Code changes are gated by tests, worktrees and rollback; a house is gated by people and presence.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: The safety invariant is structurally sound but the house-specific rule was designed (home-automation-design.md section 7 HomeRule) and not built; today a forged or mislabelled reversibility from any proposer path other than orchestration/tools.py would be honoured, and the default posture treats a door like a docstring.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Proactive behaviour is scattered and uncoordinated: curiosity.sharing -> persona.sharing -> ui.notice (text, hourly cap); execution/vision.py speaks camera descriptions on its own; kernel reminders fire; voice/session.py backchannels. None of them knows who is present, whether someone is asleep, or whether Sim is already mid-conversation.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: A single initiative policy: every unprompted utterance is a proposal scored by urgency and relevance against an interruption cost derived from the world state (who is here, activity, time, channel), with class-specific thresholds (safety alerts always, FYI only when idle, growth notes only in a digest) and channel selection by presence (voice if in the room, phone if away).
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Sim can wake a sleeping child to describe the postman, and cannot decide to text the owner instead of speaking to an empty room.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Spoken latency is 4-17 s end to end (stt 1.8-6.8 s with whisper large-v3-turbo finalising after end of turn, llm 1.3-9.5 s awaited to completion, then planner, then TTS). The voice profile (orchestration/profiles.py VOICE_CHAT) offers ~60 tools by name in free text with a 6-step marker loop and a 0.25 s memory timeout that silently drops the memory block under load.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Streaming end to end: streaming STT with early finalisation, token streaming from the model into sentence-boundary TTS, a fast lane (small or local model) for acknowledgements and simple intents, and native structured tool calls so a spoken 'turn the kitchen light off' is one function call, not a parsed marker. First-audio p50 near 1 s is the established bar.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Every second past ~1.5 s is a turn the family will not take. The marker protocol and the 8 regex police in orchestration/session.py exist because tool use is parsed from prose; native tool calling removes the class of bug and most of the latency in the tool path.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Dialogue policy is regexes and prompt prose: _WHO_SAID, _WHO_IS_SPEAKING, _I_AM, _TO_SIM in voice/session.py; addressed() heuristics in voice/backchannel.py; exchange windows and bystander logic inside the session; who_is_here prose in scaffolds.py. It lives in Voice only, so a Telegram message from the same person has none of it.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: A structured dialogue state shared across channels: each percept carries addressee (to_sim, aside, to_person X) with confidence from a small classifier, the conversation state per person (open thread, last exchange, pending question from Sim), and the model reads it as data. The same policy answers 'who said that' from the world state rather than a regex.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Every new incident becomes another regex in a 1,961-line session file; the policy cannot be measured (no labelled addressee set) or reused across channels.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: No routine learning. HA history is not read (HA not configured), no trigger engine (design section 4 never built), no procedural memory of household patterns; the persona user model learns from explicit statements only.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Routines mined from the hub's state history and presence: per (entity, service) time-of-day x weekday distributions, co-occurrence within windows (frequent-episode mining), person-conditioned preferences (temperature, brightness, volume) learnt from actual actions; proposed as suggestions, confirmed by a person, then installed as HA automations that run without Sim.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Sim cannot notice that the kitchen lights go off at 22:30 on school nights, so it cannot offer to do it, and cannot know that 23:30 with lights on is unusual.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Cameras are RTSP -> local ffmpeg -> HLS segments on disk, with stills and event JSON under workspace/cameras (3.8 GB); detection comes from the NVR's own AI kinds. Ring is a second bespoke path.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: An open-source detection and NVR layer (Frigate with go2rtc, as the design's section 1 already chose) publishes person/car/package detections with snapshots and clips over MQTT/HA; the agent consumes events and asks a vision model only about the event crop, not the whole scene.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Sim carries streaming plumbing and retention it should not own, and the 'describe the event not the scene' problem (execution/vision.py, live 2026-09-16) is what Frigate's zones and object tracking already solve.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Interface is a 10.7k-line monolith: CLI/TUI, 2,234-line command dispatch, HTTP API + dashboard + dashfeeds, Telegram, WhatsApp, TV page, benchmark views. Voice is a separate 10-11k-line subsystem that also carries dialogue policy, room memory and pronunciation. Chat sessions are throwaway (one session_id per typed line).
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Thin channel adapters (audio, CLI, Telegram, WhatsApp, web/WS, TV as an output device) that all produce the same person-resolved percept and consume the same delivery request; a separate admin/observability plane; persistent per-person conversations with a transcript and compaction.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Channel logic and admin logic change for different reasons and are tested differently; the household 'conversation' has no home because each surface owns its own.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Memory recall is hashed bag-of-words, scores every record on every call under a 0.25 s timeout; per-person filtering exists only for voice; there is no procedural/routine kind in use by the house.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Tiered memory (working transcript, episodic per person, semantic facts about people and places, procedural routines) with a real embedding index and hybrid lexical+vector retrieval; recall budgeted in tokens, not by a wall-clock race.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: The memory block that carries 'which machine is falcon' or 'Ira's bedtime' vanishes exactly when the house is busy.

target_architecture.one_paragraph: Keep the substrate exactly as it is (Bus with reserved topology, append-only Ledger, Kernel layers, Guardian as sole approver with HMAC tokens, Execution as sole actor, worktree landing for self-patches). Around it, add the three things a home agent needs and Sim lacks: a Perception subsystem that turns microphones, cameras and the Home Assistant event stream into typed, confidence-bearing percepts; a Home World State inside World Model (entity/area registry, live states, a presence belief per person per area, derived situation facts) that every prompt and every rule reads; and a People model in contracts with one person_id per family member joined across voice, Telegram, WhatsApp, CLI and HA, carrying a role tier, permissions and a memory namespace. Move the conversational policy out of voice/session.py into a cross-channel Attention and Dialogue component that labels each percept with an addressee and keeps one conversation per person; merge the four sources of unprompted speech into one Initiative policy scored against interruption cost and presence. Split the physical-action tier in Guardian onto its own axis (HomeRule recomputing classify_call, PersonRule, PresenceRule, its own auto-approve setting) while code changes keep the test-and-rollback gate. Shrink Voice to audio I/O (VAD, turns, streaming STT, sentence-chunked TTS, speaker embeddings, echo) and shrink Interface to channel adapters plus an admin plane. Replace the marker protocol with native tool calling and add a fast lane so a spoken turn answers in about a second. Learning gains a routine miner over HA history that proposes automations a person confirms and HA runs without Sim. Everything is additive to the existing packages; nothing bypasses proposal -> approval -> effect.

modules.name: Perception
modules.from: new package simorgh/perception/, built from execution/vision.py, the cam_watch/ring_watch event loops in execution/home/cameras.py and ring.py, the designed-but-unbuilt HA bridge (docs/plans/home-automation-design.md section 2.4), and Voice's transcript publication
modules.responsibility: Sensors in, typed percepts out. Owns the HA websocket subscription (state_changed, automation_triggered), camera/detection events (from the NVR today, Frigate/MQTT when adopted), the vision look at an event's frames, and the enrichment of a spoken turn (speaker, room/device, addressee guess) before it is published. Never actuates.
key_algorithms_or_methods: HA websocket client with subscribe_events(state_changed) and periodic full-state resync; each change -> percept.home.state_changed{entity_id, old, new, attributes, area, ts}

Camera event -> two stills a moment apart -> cognition.think with images and the camera's known static-scene words excluded -> percept.home.detection{camera, area, kinds, description, confidence, snapshot_ref}; move to Frigate's tracked-object events when installed so only the object crop is described
Speaker attribution as a percept field: {person_id or unknown, score, margin} from Voice's SpeakerBook, plus room/device id of the microphone
Percept dedupe and rate limits per source (a motion sensor flapping is one percept with a count, not forty)
modules.interfaces: Consumes: audio transcripts from Voice (voice.transcript), world.camera.event, HA websocket. Publishes: percept.text.received (unchanged schema plus person_id, channel, device, addressee), percept.home.state_changed, percept.home.detection, percept.presence.evidence. Requests: cognition.think (images).

modules.name: Home World State (World Model facet 'home')
modules.from: extends simorgh/worldmodel/ (new facets/home.py, facets/presence.py); absorbs voice/session.py's _room deque and contracts/places.py
modules.responsibility: The single, durable, queryable picture of the house: entity/area/device registry mirrored from HA, current entity states, per-person per-area presence belief, the last N minutes of what was said in each room, and derived situation facts (nobody_home, quiet_hours, someone_asleep, tv_playing, child_alone, alarm_state). Rendered as a compact prompt block and answered as world.env.query{what:'home'}.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Entity state table as a Ledger projection of percept.home.state_changed (rebuildable; snapshot on sleep tick), keyed by entity_id with area from HA's registry

Presence: per (person, area) belief updated by evidence likelihoods (speaker id score, HA device_tracker/router presence, motion in an area, camera person detection, a phone message from outside) with exponential time decay; report a distribution and 'unknown', never a bare name

Situation facts as small pure rules over states + presence + clock (quiet hours per household config; asleep = bedroom motion silent for T after lights off; child_alone = only child presences above threshold)
Room transcript ring per area (replaces the in-session deque) with a 3-minute horizon for asides and 48-hour overheard store from contracts/overheard.py
modules.interfaces: Consumes: percept.home.*, percept.presence.evidence, percept.text.received, voice.spoken. Replies: world.env.query{what: home|presence|room}. Publishes: world.home.situation_changed{fact, value, confidence} for rules and Initiative. Only writer of the home:state projection.

modules.name: People (identity, roles, permissions, per-person memory)
modules.from: merge of contracts/household.py + voice/speakers.py's SpeakerBook identities + interface/telegram.py and whatsapp.py allow-lists (contracts/channels.py) + persona/user_model.py, as a contracts/people.py schema with the store owned by World Model
modules.responsibility: One person_id per household member and per known guest, with linked identities (voice embedding set, Telegram id, WhatsApp number, HA person entity, CLI/owner), a role tier (owner, adult, child, guest, unknown), a permission table over tool groups and home safety classes, a memory namespace, and a preference model updated from actions as well as words.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Identity resolution at the channel edge: every adapter resolves sender -> person_id before publishing a percept; unresolved stays 'unknown' with the raw handle kept for the owner to link

Permission matrix: role x {read_only, media, reversible_home, human_home, code, memory_forget} -> allow | ask(owner) | deny; children default to media + read_only + reversible lights in their own area
Step-up verification for human-class requests by voice: speaker score >= 0.70 and margin >= 0.10 required, otherwise confirm on the person's phone channel; never from an unknown voice

Preference learning per person: exponential moving estimates of chosen brightness/temperature/volume per area from confirmed home_call results; explicit statements still via the existing facet store, now keyed by person_id
modules.interfaces: Readers: Guardian (PersonRule), Orchestration (scaffold who_is_here, memory filters), Initiative (channel selection), Memory (namespace). Writers: the owner via a people_* tool set (link identity, set role, forget person), all through Guardian.

modules.name: Attention and Dialogue Policy
modules.from: extracted from voice/session.py (_bystander, addressed/exchange window, _room_lines, _WHO_SAID/_WHO_IS_SPEAKING/_I_AM answers, backchannel) and orchestration/scaffolds.py who_is_here; new package simorgh/dialogue/ or a sub-package of orchestration
modules.responsibility: Decide, for every percept from any channel, whether it is addressed to Sim, an aside, a command, a question, or a reply to Sim's pending question; keep one open conversation per person with a bounded transcript; answer identity questions from the world state; hand a turn to Orchestration with the right profile, speaker and situation.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Addressee classification as a scored decision: name/wake mention, question shape, speaker continuity within an exchange window, whether Sim asked something of this person, gaze-less heuristics from the room record, and a fast-lane model call for ambiguous cases; output {label, confidence}, below threshold -> record as aside, never answer
Per-person conversation state (open thread id, last exchange ts, pending_question) persisted as a Ledger projection so a Telegram reply continues the kitchen conversation
Clarification policy: ask exactly when an ambiguity would change an actuation (registry Ambiguous) or when the addressee score is mid-band and the utterance is a command; otherwise stay silent
Labelled-set evaluation: the owner marks 'that was for Sim / not for Sim / wrong person' from the phone; precision/recall on that set is the module's handle
modules.interfaces: Consumes: percept.text.received (enriched). Publishes: turn.requested{person_id, channel, profile, situation} to Orchestration, dialogue.aside.recorded to World State. Replies: dialogue.who_said, dialogue.state for prompts.

modules.name: Initiative (unprompted behaviour)
modules.from: merge of curiosity/sharing.py + persona/sharing.py + execution/vision.py's announce step + delivery of kernel/scheduler.py reminders + voice backchannel greetings
modules.responsibility: The only path by which Sim speaks or messages without being asked. Scores each candidate utterance against the interruption cost implied by the home world state, picks the channel by presence, and proposes the delivery as an action so Guardian and the Ledger see it.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Utility = urgency(class) x relevance(person) - cost(activity, time, channel); classes: safety_alert (always, all channels), event_fyi (only when someone is present and not asleep, else to the owner's phone), reminder (to its person, wherever they are), growth/news (only in a requested digest or when idle with an adult present)
Presence-aware routing: voice in the area where the person is (belief > 0.6), else phone channel, else queue for the next time they address Sim

Per-person do-not-disturb windows, per-class cooldowns, and a hard daily cap; every delivery is action.proposed{tool: speak|notify, reversibility: 'attention'} so 'Sim talks too much' is a Guardian posture, not a code change
Floor coordination with the turn manager: a proactive utterance waits for LISTENING/idle and yields to any person speaking
modules.interfaces: Consumes: world.home.situation_changed, percept.home.detection, schedule.fired, curiosity.share.proposed, persona.share.proposed. Publishes: action.proposed (deliveries), initiative.suppressed{why} for measurement. Executes via existing voice.speak.request and channel send tools.

modules.name: Voice (audio I/O only)
modules.from: keep simorgh/voice/ but shrink: vad.py, turns.py, stt/, tts/, speakers.py (embeddings only), playback.py, aec.py, delivery.py, pronounce.py stay; session.py loses room memory, bystander, identity regexes and who-said answers
modules.responsibility: Microphone frames to text with speaker vectors and timing; text to speech with streaming, barge-in and echo suppression; nothing about who the person is beyond the embedding, nothing about what to say.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Streaming STT as the primary path (stt/sherpa_stream.py zipformer) with the hybrid end-of-turn using its partials; large-v3-turbo only as an offline rescoring lane for kept audio
Reply streaming: accept a token stream from Cognition, split at sentence boundaries through the planner, synthesise sentence n+1 while n plays; first audio target < 1.0 s after the reply starts
Fast lane: a canned/cached acknowledgement or a small-model one-liner when the main model is expected to exceed 2 s (predicted from the tool set requested), spoken as a bridge, never as the answer
Per-device sessions (several microphones/rooms) each with its own TurnManager, echo tracker and calibration; a device id travels on every transcript
modules.interfaces: Publishes: voice.transcript{device, text, partial|final, speaker_vector_ref, score}, voice.spoken. Consumes: voice.speak.request (now with priority and 'may_interrupt' from Initiative). Metrics per turn unchanged in voice:turns.

modules.name: Channels (thin adapters) and Admin plane
modules.from: split of simorgh/interface/: cli/tui + telegram.py + whatsapp.py + httpapi WS chat + tv page become simorgh/channels/; httpapi dashboard, dashfeeds.py, vitals.py, benchmarkview.py, panel.py become simorgh/admin/; dispatch.py becomes a command registry
modules.responsibility: Channels: resolve sender to person_id, publish the same enriched percept as voice, deliver replies and initiative messages, keep one conversation per person per channel. Admin: observe-then-control plane behind auth, where every control is itself a guarded action.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Command registry: each 'sim command' is a declared tool with a schema, callable from CLI, Telegram or voice through the same path (dispatch.py's 2,234 lines become data plus small handlers)
Persistent conversations: a session_id per (person, channel) that survives lines and restarts, with a transcript projection and compaction, replacing the throwaway session per typed line
HTTP: bind 127.0.0.1 by default, require SIM_API_TOKEN for anything but the LAN TV page; WhatsApp/Telegram webhooks verified as today
TV and Cast as output devices registered in the world state (area, capabilities) so Initiative can choose them
modules.interfaces: Publishes percept.text.received (person-resolved). Consumes turn.completed, initiative deliveries. Admin reads Ledger projections and proposes control actions through Guardian.

modules.name: Guardian (physical tier on its own axis)
modules.from: keep simorgh/guardian/; add rules from home-automation-design.md section 7 plus person and presence rules; split config
modules.responsibility: Unchanged as the sole approver. Adds a physical-action axis whose posture, auto-approve setting and rules are separate from the code-change axis.
key_algorithms_or_methods: HomeRule: for home_call, cam_*, ring_*, media/cast and any tool tagged physical, recompute classify_call from the proposal's args (never trust proposal.reversibility), apply CLIMATE_HARD_LIMITS, ALWAYS_HUMAN_SERVICES, alarm state from the world state, per-entity rate limits (no more than N toggles per minute), and 'nobody home => no unlock, no disarm'

PersonRule: requester person_id and role from the proposal against the People permission matrix; unknown or child requesting human-class -> deny with a spoken reason; adult requesting human-class -> escalate to the owner's phone with a one-tap approve that mints the token
PresenceRule: a human-class approval by voice requires the approving person to be present (belief > 0.8) and speaker-verified; otherwise the phone path

Config: [guardian.physical] auto_approve = false, irreversible_requires_human = true, independent of [guardian] used by sim.sh's SIMORGH_GUARDIAN_AUTO_APPROVE; tightening automatic (a denied unlock attempt raises posture for an hour), loosening only by the owner
modules.interfaces: Same topics; Proposal gains requester{person_id, role, channel, verified} and physical{service, entity_id, area} fields in contracts/messages/action.py.

modules.name: Execution home actuation (kept, narrowed)
modules.from: keep simorgh/execution/home/, media/, energy/; remove watchers and vision (to Perception); add automation and scene tools
modules.responsibility: Do exactly what was approved against HA and the media devices, and report what the house actually did.
key_algorithms_or_methods: home_call unchanged (before/after snapshot, undo table); add home_scene_apply and home_automation_create/enable/disable (all human class; YAML rendered from a Sim routine proposal) so learnt routines run inside HA
Registry seeded from HA's area/device registry rather than name fuzzing alone; ambiguity still refused
Camera actuation (siren, PTZ, lights) stays; streaming to the TV moves to go2rtc/Frigate URLs when adopted
Workspace retention: snapshots and HLS bounded by age and size; clips belong to the NVR
modules.interfaces: Unchanged action.approved -> action.result; new tool schemas registered as native tool definitions.

modules.name: Routine Learning (in Learning)
modules.from: new module simorgh/learning/routines.py; reads HA history via Perception's state projection; writes procedural memory
modules.responsibility: Find recurring household patterns and per-person preferences, propose them as suggestions, and hand a confirmed one to HA as an automation.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Per (entity, action) time-of-day x weekday histograms with kernel smoothing; a routine candidate when a mode has support >= 4 weeks and concentration >= 0.6 of occurrences within a 30-minute window

Episode mining: co-occurrences within a 10-minute window across entities and presence changes (arrive_home -> hallway light + thermostat) with minimum support and confidence; person-conditioned when presence attribution is confident
Anomaly flag: an expected routine that did not happen (lights still on past the learnt window with someone_asleep) becomes an Initiative candidate of class event_fyi

capability_programs.capability: Reasoning (for a household: situated reasoning over who, where, when, and what the house is doing)
capability_programs.current_state: The model reasons from persona + self summary + a memory block (hashed bag-of-words, silently dropped past 0.25 s) + the last 16 spoken lines of one microphone + a 60-tool marker list; no house state, no presence, no structured addressee; tool calls parsed from prose with 8 regex guards; one action per step; chat sessions are throwaway.
capability_programs.method: Give the model the situation as data, not prose: a compact 'house block' (areas with notable states, presence distribution, situation facts, time and quiet-hours flag) and a 'dialogue block' (who is speaking with what confidence, addressee label, open thread with this person, pending question) assembled by Orchestration from world.env.query{home, presence} and dialogue.state; native tool calling with schemas generated from the registry so a spoken command is one structured call; lane routing (fast model for ack/intent/addressee, primary for reasoning, vision for frames); a verify step for physical actions that reads home_call's before/after snapshot and says what changed. Reasoning quality then comes from the frontier model plus grounded context, which is the pattern that works in 2026: structured tool use, context management, critic loops on effects.
capability_programs.how_to_measure: A household eval set of 200 spoken/typed requests with labelled correct tool call and correct addressee (built from the ledger's voice:turns and corrected from the phone): tool-call exact-match rate, wrong-entity actuation rate (must be 0), clarification-when-ambiguous rate, and answer correctness on 'who/where/what is on' questions against the world state. Track per model in simorgh/benchmark alongside GAIA/BFCL.
capability_programs.first_increment: Implement tools= natively in cognition/providers/together.py and claude_code.py for the VOICE_CHAT profile only; generate schemas from Execution's registry; add the house block from a stub 'home' facet fed by a manual HA state dump; run the 200-case set before and after. Two weeks.

capability_programs.capability: Long tasks (household horizon: hours to weeks, e.g. 'watch the driveway tonight', 'keep the house at 21 while Soodeh is home', 'learn when we go to bed')
capability_programs.current_state: Long work exists only as code tasks with step budgets, leases and worktrees; a spoken turn is 6 steps; reminders are durable one-shots; there is no standing intent, no trigger engine (designed, unbuilt), no checkpointed monitors; a 'watch' is a tool that runs until the process dies.
capability_programs.method: Standing intents as Ledger-backed objects (design section 4's rule shape: trigger, conditions, action, expiry, owner person, class) evaluated by a small engine on percepts and situation changes, never by a model in the loop per event; each firing is a normal action.proposed with the intent as requester context; the model is used to compile a spoken request into an intent (with a read-back confirmation) and to summarise outcomes, not to poll. Long-horizon checkpointing: an intent's state (last fired, count, suppressed reasons) is a projection rebuilt on restart (Flow 7). Hard safety intents are never Sim's: they are installed into HA as automations through the human-class tool. Sub-tasks with isolated contexts (delegate exists) handle the research half of a long household job.
capability_programs.how_to_measure: Intent survival across restart (100%), firing latency from percept to action.proposed (p95 < 2 s), false firings per week on the labelled situation stream, and the fraction of standing intents that expire or are cancelled by the owner as 'annoying' (target < 10%). Ledger streams intent:<id> make all four countable.
capability_programs.first_increment: Build the intent object and engine over the existing schedule stream plus percept.home.state_changed, with three intents: 'tell me when someone is at the front door after 22:00', 'lights off in the kitchen when nobody has been there for 20 minutes', 'remind Aran at 20:30 on school nights'; all firings through Guardian; two weeks after the HA bridge exists.

capability_programs.capability: Environment interaction (Home Assistant as the hub, cameras and events as perception, actuation gated by people and presence)
capability_programs.current_state: Five home_* tools over HA REST (HA not configured), Reolink/Ring tools with bespoke watchers, ffmpeg HLS relays, Cast/Android TV tools; classify_call exists but Guardian does not recompute it; no HA event ingestion; no presence; cameras described whole-scene by a vision model.
capability_programs.method: Perception subsystem with an HA websocket bridge (state_changed -> percepts) and a full-state resync; Frigate/go2rtc for detection and streams with Sim consuming tracked-object events; a home world state projection with presence belief fusion (speaker id, device trackers, motion, detections, decay); Guardian HomeRule/PersonRule/PresenceRule on a separate physical axis with its own auto-approve default false; home_call unchanged in shape (ambiguity refused, before/after snapshot, undo); automation create/enable/disable as human-class tools so routines run inside HA; registry seeded from HA's area/device registry. Every physical effect remains proposal -> approval -> effect.
capability_programs.how_to_measure: Percept lag from HA state change to projection (p95 < 500 ms on LAN); presence accuracy against a one-week diary the family corrects from the phone (per-person area accuracy > 85%, unknown reported rather than wrong); actuation correctness on the eval set (wrong entity 0, refused-ambiguous rate); human-class attempts that reached Execution without a person's approval (must be 0, with a self-check drill like the forged-token one); camera announcements judged 'described the event, not the scene' > 90%.
capability_programs.first_increment: Install HA on a separate box per the design, configure HOME_ASSISTANT_URL/TOKEN, add the Guardian HomeRule that imports classify_call and recomputes from args, add [guardian.physical] with auto_approve=false, and add a kernel self-check drill that proposes lock.unlock with reversibility='reversible' and asserts it is escalated. One week; it closes the most serious gap before anything else grows.

capability_programs.capability: User interaction (turn taking, barge-in, latency, several people, when to speak unprompted, when to ask)
capability_programs.current_state: Solid turn manager and barge-in gate; 4-17 s spoken responses; addressee and identity by regex inside voice/session.py; no per-person conversation across channels; proactive speech from four uncoordinated sources; bystander suppression by exchange windows; children handled by prompt prose; no labelled data for any of it.
capability_programs.method: Latency: streaming STT primary, LLM token streaming into sentence-boundary TTS, fast-lane acknowledgements, native tool calls; target first audio p50 <= 1.2 s, p95 <= 2.5 s from end of speech for tool-free turns. Turn taking: keep the state machine, add a HOLD state for initiative and per-device sessions. Addressee: a scored classifier over name mention, question shape, exchange continuity, pending question, with a fast-model tie-break; below threshold means silence. Identity: People model with speaker verification scores and step-up on the phone for human-class requests. Proactivity: Initiative policy with interruption cost from presence/activity/time, presence-aware channel choice, class thresholds, daily caps, every delivery a guarded action. Asking: ask only when the answer changes an actuation or the addressee is mid-band on a command; otherwise act or stay quiet. Children: role tier limits tools and initiative classes, not just tone.
capability_programs.how_to_measure: From voice:turns and the new labelled streams: first-audio p50/p95 per turn class; addressee precision/recall (target > 0.9/0.85) on a 500-line labelled set including asides and cross-talk; speaker misattribution rate (< 2%, unknown allowed); false-interruption rate from barge-in (crow-and-TV set); unprompted utterances per day per person and the fraction the family marks unwanted (< 10%); clarification questions per actuation request (bounded, not zero).
capability_programs.first_increment: Wire cognition.think.partial -> planner -> StreamingSynthesiser so Sim speaks the first sentence while the model is still writing, and make sherpa streaming the primary STT with whisper as the rescoring lane; measure first_audio before and after on the same 50 spoken turns. Two weeks; it is the change the family notices most.

capability_programs.capability: Self-improvement (for a household: learning routines, preferences and identities safely, plus the existing code-level path)
capability_programs.current_state: Code self-patching works (worktree, gate, rollback); competence table per task type; curiosity explores the codebase; persona learns two regex facets; the speaker book refines voices under strict rules; nothing learns from the house; the self model's capabilities['tools'] is never written; reflection observes but does not act.
capability_programs.method: Three learning loops with different gates. (1) Routine mining from HA history and presence (time-of-day x weekday histograms, windowed episode mining, person-conditioned preferences) producing suggestions with a proposed -> shown -> accepted/declined lifecycle; accepted routines become HA automations through a human-class tool, so learning changes the house only with a person's yes and runs without Sim afterwards. (2) Identity and preference refinement from confirmed events (speaker takes from verified solo turns as today; brightness/temperature/volume estimates from confirmed home_call results; corrections from the phone as labelled data). (3) Code self-patching as today, but driven by the household handles: an eval-driven loop where a regression in addressee precision or first-audio p95 opens a patch task with the failing cases attached. Reflection's findings feed the Self Model's competence per household task type (actuation, identification, announcement) so Initiative and Guardian posture can read 'I misidentify voices in the car'. Loosening any gate stays human-only.
capability_programs.how_to_measure: Routine suggestions accepted / shown (target > 40% after a month), routines later disabled by the owner (< 15%); preference estimate error on held-out actions; speaker-book precision over time; the household eval set's scores per release (no metric may drop across a bless); number of learning-driven changes that reached HA without a person's approval (0).
capability_programs.first_increment: After four weeks of HA history exists: the histogram miner over light/switch/climate events with a weekly digest of at most three suggestions delivered through Initiative to the owner only; accepted ones rendered as HA automation YAML and installed via the human-class tool. Three weeks including the tool.

result.agi_honesty: Plainly: this architecture is a harness around a frontier model, and its reasoning ceiling is that model's. It can become a highly competent, trustworthy, continuously improving household agent, and 'more general' has a concrete meaning here that is worth investing in: (1) it handles requests nobody wrote a feature for by composing a large, honest tool surface over one device hub with a world state it can actually read; (2) it treats a family as several people with their own memory, permissions and preferences rather than one user; (3) it acts on its own initiative with judgment about presence, time and interruption; (4) it learns the household's routines and installs them where they run without it; (5) it improves its own code against measured household handles with a gate and rollback. Those five compound: every new HA integration, every corrected identification, every accepted routine and every labelled turn makes the next request easier. What it cannot become: a self-contained general intelligence. There is no weight-level learning; 'self-improvement' is memory, skills, routines and audited code; perception is limited to microphones, cameras and hub state; embodiment is limited to what HA can actuate; and its judgment on novel situations is bounded by the cloud model's, filtered through a context this architecture assembles. The regex police, prompt prose and marker protocol do not compound and should not be mistaken for intelligence work. If 'AGI' is used at all for this project it should stay as the blueprint's own stance (01 section 2.1): a queryable competence and calibration per household task type in the Ledger, never a claim. A useful honest target for 2027 is 'the most trustworthy agent in this house': zero unapproved physical effects, sub-second first audio, presence and addressee accuracy the family stops noticing, and routines it learnt that still run when it is switched off.
result.biggest_risk_of_this_proposal: That the house layer grows before the identity and physical-safety layers do. A presence-aware, proactive agent with today's identity model (three unjoined per-channel identities, no requester on proposals, Guardian trusting the proposer's reversibility label, one auto-approve knob covering doors and docstrings, speaker id that once filed the creator under Aran) is a safety problem, not a feature: a misidentified voice plus 'trusted' mode is a child unlocking the front door. So stage 0 and stage 1 are prerequisites, not options, and the whole program depends on Home Assistant actually being installed, which the design has said for nine days and nobody has done. The second risk is the same one the codebase has already met twelve times: designed slots with one side built (the home subsystem, the trigger engine, the HomeRule, the People model) left as unconnected wires because coding agents build the half that is easy to unit test. The mitigation is the project's own lesson: every stage ends with one watched live run of the primary interface (a spoken turn in the kitchen, a Telegram message from outside) and a number read from the Ledger, and a stage that cannot show its handle moving does not get blessed.

result.lens: The modern agent harness (2026 coding/computer-use agent shape): one agent loop over a typed turn transcript, native structured tool use with JSON-schema tools, parallel tool calls, streaming deltas, token-pressure compaction with protected prefix, hooks (pre/post tool, stop, pre-compact, session-start), declarative agent definitions as permission modes, sub-agents with isolated context, skills as procedural memory, resumable sessions. Applied to Simorgh with one non-negotiable: Guardian stays the mandatory PreToolUse hook for every effect (action.proposed -> HMAC-approved -> Execution), and corrigibility (pause/stop/human gate) stays structural.

what_sim_got_right.decision: The action path is structural: action.proposed -> Guardian (12 ordered rules, HMAC token) -> action.approved -> Execution (re-verifies token) -> action.result, with the subscribe/publish invariants enforced by the Bus and proved at boot (contracts/topics.py SUBSCRIBE_ONLY_BY/PUBLISH_ONLY_BY, kernel/selfcheck.py).
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Every 2026 harness has a permission layer; almost all implement it as convention inside the loop (a hook callback the loop may forget to call). Sim's is a bus topology no code path can bypass, and it is exactly the shape a parallel-tool-call, sub-agent, self-modifying agent needs: N tool_use blocks in one turn become N proposals, each independently gated, and a child agent cannot inherit an approval. This is the one part of the design that becomes MORE valuable as autonomy grows.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep byte-for-byte. Make it the loop's mandatory PreToolUse hook (the harness cannot construct a ToolResult for an external tool except from an action.result). Extend Guardian's protected paths to the new agent-definition directory and the hooks package, since those now hold permission posture (principle 4.11: loosening is human-only).

what_sim_got_right.decision: Append-only Ledger as the only truth, with projections rebuilt from it; task:<id> streams; orchestration/resume.py distinguishing a crash (continue the attempt) from a retry (new budget, carried memory of earlier attempts).
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Resumable, checkpointed long-horizon sessions are the defining property of long-task agents. Sim already has the substrate (durable step events, lease heartbeat, worker-agnostic resume); what it lacks is that the transcript itself is not on the ledger. Once the session transcript is a stream, resume, replay, audit, eval-from-traces and compaction all read the same data.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Strengthen: add a session:<id> stream (typed turns) as the unit of persistence for chat, tasks and sub-agents alike; snapshot every N events. Fix the cost side separately (fsync per append and one trace stream per message are what made 118k stream files).

what_sim_got_right.decision: Contracts-only import rule, 175 typed topics, 174 JSON schemas, one package per subsystem; only Kernel composes.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: This is what makes the re-architecture below feasible incrementally: moving orchestration+cognition into one agent package changes no other subsystem, and replacing Memory's internals is invisible to everyone. It is also what lets coding agents work on modules in parallel (the creator's actual development style).
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep. Stop using it as the reason tool descriptions do not reach the model: tool.registered already carries description and args_schema across the bus, so the boundary was never the blocker.

what_sim_got_right.decision: Profiles (per-kind tool allowlists, step budgets, verify flag, scaffold text) plus per-profile scaffolds rendered into a protected task_rules block; a 'chat' profile that can write files, install packages and start tasks.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: This is the harness pattern of declarative agent definitions / permission modes (an agent = tools + model + budget + system prompt + isolation). Sim reached it from the other side, one live-caught incident at a time, and the content of those scaffolds is hard-won and correct.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Strengthen into files: agents/<name>.md with frontmatter (tools, model_tier, max_turns, max_cost_usd, max_wall_s, max_parallel_tools, verify, isolation, compaction thresholds) and the scaffold as body; Guardian-protected; loaded by Kernel. profiles.py and scaffolds.py become the loader.

what_sim_got_right.decision: Skills in the open Agent Skills format (SKILL.md with frontmatter; catalog of name+description in every task; body loaded only on use_skill), discovered from configured roots, per-profile allowlists.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Procedural memory as files the model can read, the creator can diff, and Guardian can protect is the pattern that scales capability without code: a skill is cheaper, safer and more transferable than a tool or a subsystem. It is also the natural OUTPUT of a self-improvement loop.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep. Make skills the primary artifact the growth layer produces (reflection/distillation.py already drafts them) and gate promotion on an eval delta, not on a model's opinion.

what_sim_got_right.decision: In-process delegation (`delegate`): a child Session with fresh context, its own small budget, read-only research profile, summary-only return, depth cap, and tier escalation when a helper fails.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Sub-agents with isolated context are how 2026 harnesses keep the parent's context clean and parallelize exploration; running the child in-process (not through the task queue) is the right call for a one-worker deployment and avoids the self-deadlock the design doc identified.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Generalize into a `Task(agent, brief, isolation, budget)` built-in tool that can spawn any agent definition (research, verify, planner, skill-writer), concurrently up to a cap, each on its own session stream.

what_sim_got_right.decision: Progress-note re-grounding (goal / done / learned / next / open questions as a structured JSON note) replacing the transcript every N steps, forced on context_too_large, and carried across attempts.
what_sim_got_right.why_it_matters_for_the_future: Structured summaries with a preserved 'next' are the compaction strategy that actually works for long tasks (a free-form summary loses the plan). Sim already has the right note shape.
what_sim_got_right.keep_or_strengthen: Keep the note; change the trigger from step count to measured token pressure, precede it with cheaper tool-result aging, and apply it to chat sessions too.

what_sim_got_right.decision: Cognition router: ordered failover with per-provider rolling budgets replayed from the ledger, shared deadline slices, cooldown circuit breaker, truncation retry, purpose filters, image-capability filter, tier escalation (strong tier on attempt N or helper failure).

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Tool calls are parsed out of free text by a marker protocol: `NAME: argument` on its own line, one string argument, a JSON-second-line hack for multi-field tools, a hand-maintained _CODE_BEARING_MARKERS set that has been wrong every time a tool was added, and tool_hints as prose. Every provider adapter ignores tools=. Execution tools already declare JSON args_schema and descriptions; both are thrown away before the model sees them. MCP tools with more than one property cannot be called at all (mcp_single_arg_key).
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Native structured tool use: the model receives ToolSpec{name, description, input_schema} in the provider's dialect (OpenAI-style functions for Together/Ollama, Anthropic tools, Gemini function declarations), emits typed tool_use blocks with JSON input validated against the schema, and receives tool_result blocks keyed by the call id. The ProviderResponse.tool_calls field already exists and is never filled.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: This single divergence is the root of the session.py regex-police family (invented_markers, unhonoured_marker, _transcript_echo, claimed_to_commit, promised_behaviour, claimed_tv_act, claimed_to_note_a_pronunciation), of the 246-tool-runs-without-a-write incident, of the first-line-argument truncations, of multi-arg tools being unreachable, and of a measurable BFCL ceiling. With schemas, an unknown tool is a schema error not a regex catch, a multi-line payload is a JSON string, and 'narrating a call' has no syntax to leak through.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: A CLI chat turn is a throwaway Session: interface mints a fresh session_id per typed line; no transcript; continuity = memory recall (two or three bus requests, 0.25 s, bag-of-words), which the code itself documents losing 'falcon/sparrow' and giving two different birthdays two turns apart.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: One persistent, resumable session per (channel, person) with an append-only typed transcript that is compacted, not discarded; memory recall augments the transcript instead of standing in for it.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Multi-turn coherence, corrections, 'what did I just say', and resumption after restart all depend on this. It is also why chat cannot be compacted (nothing to compact) and why the per-turn recall must be so aggressive.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Prompt assembly is split across two subsystems (cognition/assembler.py: constitution, persona voice, self summary, user profile, task_rules; orchestration/context.py: memory block, task, carried notes, messages), each block fetched by a bus request with a 0.25 s timeout, silently omitted on timeout, with the ordering unstable per turn.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: One ContextBuilder inside the loop with an explicit token budget per section, a stable prefix order (constitution -> persona -> self summary -> tools -> skills catalog -> transcript) for provider prompt caching, and per-turn variable material (memory recall) placed inside the latest user turn so the cached prefix survives.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Today the prompt silently changes shape under load (the memory block vanishing is 'the normal case, not an edge' per the code) and no prefix is cacheable, so every call pays full input price and latency.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Memory: hashed bag-of-words embeddings (sha256 token buckets, 256 dims) because the real embedder costs 24.9 s on first call; an inverted index made hashing recall fast (21 ms at 10k), but relevance is vocabulary overlap; working memory exists and is never fed; semantic memory is free-text distillations, with contradiction handling by header prose ('later lines win').
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Tiered memory: working (the transcript), episodic (turn records with real dense embeddings in a local index), semantic (a fact store with explicit supersession chains per person/subject/attribute), procedural (skills); hybrid retrieval (BM25 + dense, reciprocal-rank fusion, recency/person/confidence rerank); retrieval also exposed to the model as a tool for agentic recall.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Recall quality is the ceiling on 'knows the family across months'. A correction should win by data structure (superseded_by), not by asking the model to notice which line is later.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: One action per step, except a batch of read-only markers; tool results bounded at 8,000 chars by a class constant; compaction triggered by step count (reground every N) and only for non-chat; Cognition's five-layer compaction pipeline operates on flat message dicts with no turn structure.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: A step is one model turn that may contain N tool_use blocks (reads run concurrently, writes serialize in order); compaction driven by measured tokens against the model's window: first age out old tool_result content into re-fetchable stubs, then a structured summary of everything but the protected prefix and the last M turns; applies to every session kind.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Long tasks spend steps on things that should be one turn, and hit context_too_large before the reground fires; chat never compacts at all.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: No streaming anywhere: providers return whole completions (Together via to_thread), Voice waits 1.3-9.5 s for the full reply before planning TTS; measured full response 4-17 s.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Provider stream() yielding text and tool_use deltas; the harness publishes deltas to surfaces; Voice's existing StreamingSynthesiser/StreamingPlayer consume sentence-sized chunks as they arrive; a tool_use start triggers a short spoken filler.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Time-to-first-audio is the dominant felt latency for the family, and the last stage of the voice pipeline is already built for streaming input it never receives.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Growth is three subsystems: Learning (its PatchPipeline is unreachable: no publisher for learn.pipeline.run, and draft_candidate is not a registered tool; health reports degraded), Reflection (observer only, drafts skills to a directory), Curiosity (idle-tick exploration). Self Model is in-memory per process, capabilities['tools'] never written.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: One eval-driven improvement loop: review traces and benchmark failures -> produce skills, memory facts, and config/prompt proposals -> land them through the same gated loop (worktree + suite + evals) -> update a Self Model that is a fold of ledger streams (tool registry, benchmark history, outcomes).
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Self-improvement currently happens only when the creator types `improve`; the designed autonomous path does not run. Merging the three into one service with one output type (a proposal through the harness) is what makes the growth layer real.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Regex police in session.py as the honesty mechanism: each a live-caught incident turned into a heuristic, each with a once-per-session correction turn, all specific to marker-era failure modes.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: One generic Stop hook: 'the assistant's final text claims an effect and this turn has no tool_result from a mutating tool' -> bounce once with the list of tools that could do it; plus Verification's trajectory check for tasks.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: The heuristics are unbounded in number and cost a correction turn each; with structured tool use most of their trigger conditions cannot occur.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Cognition is a bus service that assembles prompts, parses markers, compacts and routes; Orchestration is a bus service that runs the loop; the loop talks to its own brain by bus request with a think timeout.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: The loop owns context, parsing and compaction (they are loop concerns); the LLM layer is a library gateway (routing, budgets, streaming, dialects, token counting) injected into the loop; the bus carries effects, events, perception and surfaces, not the loop's inner monologue.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Today a think is a bus round-trip carrying the whole prompt as a payload (and every message gets a trace stream); the 300 s handler timeout was once every task's wall budget. The bus is the right instrument for effects and events, the wrong one for a synchronous, streaming, large-payload call inside one process.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: interface/dispatch.py: 2,234 lines of command dispatch, a separate command language from the model's tools, bridged by a `sim_command` tool that routes model text back into CLI dispatch.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Slash commands are skills or tools the same loop uses; the TUI renders the session stream (the same typed turns the ledger holds); operator commands stay as a thin shell.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: Two vocabularies drift; the model reaches operator functions through a string tunnel with no schema.

where_it_diverges_from_the_future.current: Tests: 447 files / 90k lines, asserting code shape; the project's own review says they missed every real blocker; real signal came from watched single-task trials and observer waves.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.future_pattern: Eval-driven development: a small scenario suite (recorded provider fixtures for determinism, a live-gated tier for real models) plus the benchmark unit as the merge gate; unit tests only where the logic is pure.
where_it_diverges_from_the_future.gap: The migration below cannot be done safely with the current gate; the trial suite must be promoted first.

target_architecture.one_paragraph: Keep the substrate (Bus, Ledger, Kernel, Contracts) and the safety path (Guardian, Execution with its token verifier, Verification, worktree landing, simloader) exactly as they are. Collapse the thinking path -- orchestration (session, context, profiles, scaffolds, tools mapping, progress, resume, worker) plus cognition's assembler, parser, compaction and the marker protocol -- into one `agent/` package: a single Harness loop over a typed, ledger-persisted turn transcript, native JSON-schema tools rendered per provider dialect, parallel tool_use blocks (reads concurrent, writes serialized), streaming deltas to surfaces, token-pressure compaction with a protected prefix, hooks (PreToolUse = Guardian proposal, mandatory; PostToolUse; Stop; PreCompact; SessionStart), declarative agent definitions as permission modes, and a `Task` built-in for isolated sub-agents. Cognition shrinks to an `llm/` gateway (providers, router, budgets, tiers, streaming, tokens, cache-aware ordering) injected into the loop by the Kernel through a contracts protocol, the same way bus and ledger clients are. Memory becomes four real tiers with a dense index and a fact store with supersession. Learning, Reflection and Curiosity merge into one `improve/` service whose only output is proposals through the same harness (skills, memory facts, config/prompt PRs), scored by evals. The Bus remains the fabric for effects (action.*), tool registry, task lifecycle, perception, surfaces, growth events, system control and multi-process mode -- not for prompt-block RPC.

modules.name: agent (the Harness)
modules.from: merge of orchestration/{session,context,profiles,scaffolds,tools,progress,resume,worker,claims} + cognition/{assembler,parser,compaction} + the marker protocol (kept as a fallback dialect)
modules.responsibility: Run one loop for every session kind (chat, voice-chat, task, project, sub-agent): build context, stream the model, execute tool_use blocks through Guardian, append typed turns to the session stream, compact under token pressure, delegate, stop; resume any session from its stream.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Turn model: Session{id, agent, channel, person, parent_id, depth, budget{turns, tokens, cost_usd, wall_s}, state}; Turn{seq, role: system|user|assistant|tool, blocks[], ts, meta{provider, model, in_tokens, out_tokens, cost}}; Block = Text | ToolUse{id, name, input} | ToolResult{tool_use_id, content, is_error, ref, bytes_total} | Image{ref}. Persisted as ledger stream session:<id> with events session.turn.appended / session.compacted{summary, dropped_seq_range} / session.snapshot; state = fold of the stream.

Loop: while not stopped: check pause/cancel -> ContextBuilder.build(session) -> llm.stream(...) -> collect assistant turn -> if no tool_use: Stop hooks (claimed-effect check, Verification for task agents with bounded revise) -> done; else partition tool_use blocks: read-only set run concurrently via asyncio.gather over propose_and_await, mutating list run sequentially in block order stopping at first is_error; append ONE tool turn with N ToolResult blocks in the original order; budgets checked in turns, tokens, USD and wall-clock; last-turn and winding-down hints kept from today's assembler.

PreToolUse hook (mandatory, not configurable): ToolUse -> action.proposed{action_id = tool_use.id, tool, args = input (schema-validated), scope, reversibility, session_id, agent} -> await action.approved|denied|needs_human -> Execution -> action.result -> ToolResult. Denial becomes ToolResult{is_error: true, content: 'denied by <rule>: <reason>'} so the model adapts. needs_human parks the session (state = awaiting_human, event on the stream) and resumes on ui reply. Built-in tools with no external effect (Task, use_skill, memory_search, recall_result, plan/todo) bypass Guardian exactly as delegate/use_skill do today, and are the only ones that may.

ToolRegistryView: ToolSpec{name, description, input_schema (JSON Schema object), reversibility, network, cost_class, source: execution|mcp:<server>|builtin, tags} folded from tool.registered (replayed at boot, as service.py already does); jsonschema validation before proposing (stdlib-only validator for the subset used, or the optional jsonschema package); unknown name -> ToolResult{is_error}. Marker dialect retained only for providers whose capability flag says supports_tools = false (floor, Claude CLI wrapper, tool-less local models).

Agent definitions: agents/<name>.md, frontmatter {tools: allowlist with globs like 'mcp:*' and 'cam_*', model_tier, max_turns, max_cost_usd, max_wall_s, max_parallel_tools, verify, isolation: fresh|fork, compaction: {age_results_at: 0.7, summarize_at: 0.85, keep_recent_turns: 6}, channels}, body = the scaffold text. Guardian-protected directory. Replaces profiles.py + scaffolds.py; today's CHAT/PATCH/RESEARCH/SKILL/VOICE_CHAT become five files.

ContextBuilder: fixed prefix order for prompt caching -- constitution, persona voice, self summary, user profile, agent body, tool specs, skills catalog -- then the compacted transcript; per-turn variable material (memory recall block, environment notices, time) injected as a block at the head of the latest user turn, never in the prefix. Section token budgets, explicit; unavailable sections rendered as an honest note (kept from context.py). Reads persona/self/memory through injected read protocols (in-process in single mode), not 0.25 s bus RPCs.

Compactor: measure tokens (provider count when available, estimate otherwise) against the model window. Layer A (age_results_at): ToolResult content older than keep_recent_turns replaced by a stub '[result of <tool> <args-preview>, <N> chars, ref session:<id>#<seq>]' that the model can re-fetch with recall_result. Layer B (summarize_at): today's ProgressNote (goal/done/learned/next/open questions) written by a cheap purpose over everything except the protected prefix and the last M turns; chat uses a 'conversation so far' flavour with facts-about-people preserved. PreCompact hook lets the agent definition add 'preserve X'. session.compacted event; the ledger keeps everything.

Delegation: built-in Task{agent, brief, isolation: fresh|fork(last K turns), budget} -> child Session on its own session stream, run in-process (never via the task queue, so a one-worker deployment cannot deadlock), depth <= max_depth, concurrency <= max_children; returns final text bounded as a ToolResult; tier escalation on helper failure kept. Projects = a parent session whose plan step spawns children and awaits them; Planning's DAG scheduler orders them.

Hooks: SessionStart (resume from stream; carried attempt notes), UserPromptSubmit (memory recall injection; person/channel tagging), PreToolUse (Guardian; budget; pause), PostToolUse (side-effect record: uncommitted files, created paths, write-watch), Stop (claimed-effect-without-tool bounce once; Verification for verify: true agents with bounded revise), PreCompact. Implemented as an ordered list per agent definition; the Guardian hook cannot be removed.

Streaming: llm.stream yields Delta{text | tool_use_start{id,name} | tool_use_input_json | stop{reason}}; the harness publishes session.delta on the bus (bus-only, not ledgered) for the TUI, HTTP feed and Voice; the completed turn is what reaches the ledger. Cancellation on system.stop drops the stream and records a truncated turn honestly.

Budgets and resume: turn/token/USD/wall-clock per attempt from the agent definition or the task; resume.py logic kept (crash = continue, retry = new budget with carried note), now reading the session stream instead of task.step summaries.
modules.interfaces: Consumes: task.available (claim), percept.text.received / voice turns (open or continue a session), action.approved|denied|needs_human|result (by action_id), tool.registered, system.pause|stop|resume, ui.reply. Produces: action.proposed, task.started|step|progress|completed|failed|blocked, turn.completed, session.delta (bus-only), memory.store. Injected protocols from Kernel: Llm (stream/complete/count_tokens/tiers), MemoryReader, SelfModelReader, PersonaReader, Ledger, Bus. Unlocks: BFCL and BFCL-parallel as a direct measure; steps per task down; correction turns per 100 turns to ~0; resume after kill -9 mid-task; TTFT visible in the TUI.

modules.name: llm (provider gateway)
modules.from: cognition minus assembler/parser/compaction: providers/, router.py, budget.py, tokens.py, api.py
modules.responsibility: Turn (system, messages, tools, budget, purpose, tier) into a streamed model response in the right provider dialect, with routing, failover, budgets and cost accounting; no prompt assembly, no parsing of prose.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Provider protocol: capabilities{supports_tools, supports_streaming, supports_images, context_window, cache_prefix} + stream(system, messages, tools, max_tokens, timeout, reasoning_effort) -> AsyncIterator[Delta]; complete() derived from stream.

Dialect adapters: Together (OpenAI-compatible chat completions with tools/tool_choice and streaming; confident the API supports it, per-model support must be measured -- flag: the current low-cost model's tool-calling quality is unknown until benchmarked), Ollama (chat API tools for tool-capable models), Gemini (function declarations), a direct Anthropic Messages API adapter when a key is configured (tool_use/tool_result blocks, streaming, prompt caching); the Claude Code CLI wrapper stays text-only and is marked supports_tools = false.

Router kept: ordered failover, shared deadline slices, cooldown, truncation retry, billable-on-failure, purpose filters; add tier selection by task class (chat/default, code/strong, verdict/cheap) with escalation rules already present; per-purpose reasoning_effort.
Token counting per provider where offered, estimate otherwise; cache-aware: report cached_input_tokens (field exists) and expose prefix-stability hints to the ContextBuilder.
Floor provider kept as the deterministic last resort, now answering with an honest text-only turn and never a tool_use.
modules.interfaces: A library injected into agent/ and improve/ via contracts.protocols.Llm; also still answers cognition.think on the bus for other subsystems (Planning decomposer, Memory consolidation, Verification checklist) until they are moved to the injected protocol. Produces cognition.provider.status, budget metrics. Unlocks: tokens/$ per purpose with cache hits; TTFT.

modules.name: memory
modules.from: keep package; rebuild store internals (store.py, recall.py, embed.py, consolidation.py)
modules.responsibility: Four tiers -- working (the session transcript, owned by agent/), episodic (turn records), semantic (facts with supersession), procedural (skills) -- with hybrid retrieval and a model-callable search tool.
key_algorithms_or_methods: Embeddings: a small sentence-embedding model (MiniLM-class, ~384 dims) loaded in a background thread at boot; hashing remains the floor until it is warm and forever when the optional dependency is absent; every record stores which embedder produced its vector (already the convention).

Index: a numpy matrix per kind with brute-force cosine (sub-10 ms to ~100k records); an ANN library only if the store passes ~200k; BM25 over a stdlib inverted index; hybrid via reciprocal rank fusion; rerank by recency half-life, person tag, confidence, contradiction penalty (all existing signals); optional cheap-model rerank of the top 20 for chat.

Fact store (semantic tier): Fact{id, person, subject, attribute, value, ts, source_ref (session:<id>#<seq>), confidence, superseded_by}; extraction at turn end by a cheap purpose ('extract durable facts about people, places, devices, preferences'); supersession by key (person, subject, attribute); recall renders 'X (was Y until <date>)' so a correction wins by structure.
Consolidation on system.tick.sleep kept: episodic -> facts + skill candidates; the live-caught 'answered instead of summarised' guard kept.
Agentic recall: memory_search{query, kinds, person, since} exposed as a built-in tool so the model can look again when the injected block is not enough.
modules.interfaces: Consumes turn.completed, memory.store/forget; answers MemoryReader (in-process) and memory.retrieve (bus). Produces memory.stored/consolidated/contradiction.flagged. Unlocks: recall@k on a scripted 30-turn household eval; the 'falcon/sparrow' and 'birthday correction' cases pass by construction.

modules.name: substrate: bus, ledger, kernel, contracts

capability_programs.current_state: One think per step at low reasoning effort on the cheapest Together model; tool calls parsed from prose (a parse tax on every step); no plan/act/critique separation inside a task except Verification at the end; tier escalation only on attempt N or helper failure; BFCL/GAIA/SWE-bench scored but not gating anything.
capability_programs.method: (1) Native structured tool use removes the parse tax and the correction turns. (2) Router picks tier and reasoning effort by task class at the first call (chat: default/low; code/patch: strong or extended reasoning; verdicts: cheap), with today's escalation kept. (3) Plan-then-act for task agents: a `planner` sub-agent writes a typed plan with acceptance criteria; the executing agent keeps a plan/todo block in the protected prefix and updates it with the built-in plan tool. (4) Critic loop: Verification as the Stop hook with max_revisions bounded revise; for high-rigor tasks a fresh-context `verify` sub-agent reviews the diff and trajectory. (5) Self-consistency only for verdict purposes (3 cheap samples, majority), never for drafts.
