result.agi_honesty: An architecture like this -- a frontier model called through a harness with tools, tiered memory, sub-agents, skills and a gated self-improvement loop -- does not become AGI by architecture. Its general intelligence is the model's; the harness decides how much of it reaches the world, how reliably, for how long, and how safely. Nothing here learns weights, and no amount of loop design gives Sim competence the model it calls does not have. What this architecture CAN deliver, and what 'more general' concretely means for a household agent: (1) coverage -- a rising fraction of the family's real goals completable end-to-end (files, web, calendar, mail, home devices, TV, cameras, code) without the creator stepping in, measured by a scripted household eval; (2) horizon -- tasks that span hours, restarts and human interruptions with the same safety profile, measured by resume and long-task evals; (3) transfer -- a skill or fact learned in one task helping on a held-out one, measured by A/B on the trial suite; (4) continuity -- knowing the family across months with corrections that stick; (5) breadth of environment -- new capability arriving as MCP servers and skills rather than subsystems. What compounds: the eval suite, the memory substrate, the skills library, the ledger of transcripts (every future eval and distillation reads it), and the model upgrades that a clean native-tool gateway makes free. What does not compound: more regex police, more bespoke command dispatch, more subsystems, and any growth mechanism not scored by an eval. The honest framing the blueprint already adopts is the right one: generality is a queryable number in the Ledger, and the Self Model should report it, including what Sim still cannot do. Two limits to state plainly: the loop cannot verify its own honesty without external checks (Verification, evals, the creator), and corrigibility must stay outside anything the improve loop can touch -- which this proposal keeps by Guardian-protecting agent definitions, hooks and the eval gate.
result.biggest_risk_of_this_proposal: That it becomes a second rewrite. One developer, ~87k lines, a 90k-line test suite that asserts shape and missed every real blocker, and a plan that moves the loop, the brain gateway and the protocol. If Stage 4 (the package consolidation) is attempted before Stage 0 (a gate that catches loop breakage) or alongside Stage 2 (protocol change), weeks of green tests can hide a broken agent, and the live checkout is what boots the family's assistant. Mitigation is procedural and non-negotiable: one stage in flight at a time, each landed through the worktree path with trial-suite and benchmark deltas recorded in docs/findings/, file moves separated from behaviour changes, and the marker protocol kept as a per-provider fallback until native tool use beats it on BFCL for the model actually in use. The secondary risk is specific: the low-cost Together model's native tool-calling quality is unmeasured and may be worse than markers; measure per model before flipping the default, and configure a second native-tool provider so the harness is not judged by one model's quirks.

best_ideas_to_graft: Native structured tool use behind a per-provider capability flag with the marker protocol kept as the fallback dialect, gated per model on BFCL and the trial suite before the default flips (the Together GLM-5.3-Flash model's tool-calling quality is unmeasured; this is the right way to find out).

cross_cutting_disagreements: ORDER OF NATIVE TOOL CALLING: harness puts it at stage 2, systems at stage 1, embodied at stage 3 (voice profile first), cognitive last at stage 6. Harness/systems are right. Every provider adapter ignores tools= and cognition/service.py passes tools=None (verified), which is the root of the seven regex police and of MCP tools with more than one property being uncallable (mcp_single_arg_key returns None). Cognitive's own checkpoint critic and growth loop mine trajectories whose tool results can today be fabricated as text; its text concedes 'a critic cannot be trusted while results can be echoed'. Native tools must land before any loop that learns from trajectories, but AFTER a gate exists and per model on BFCL, with markers as the fallback dialect.

RE-GROUNDING TRIGGER: cognitive says switch on reground_every_steps=3 (the spec's number); harness says trigger on measured token pressure after aging tool results into re-fetchable stubs; systems says compact the thread with cognition's layers 1-5. Harness is right and cognitive is contradicted by data: docs/findings/2026-09-15 measured every-6 as no gain with ~2x 'step budget exhausted' and says every-10/keep-4 if retried. Graft cognitive's independent idea (the model's progress note becomes the carried note across attempts, replacing the mechanical 220-char-per-step summary) without its trigger.

WHERE THE BRAIN CALL LIVES: harness makes cognition an injected llm/ library and moves assembler/parser/compaction into the loop; cognitive, systems and embodied keep cognition.think as a bus RPC and the two packages separate. Harness's diagnosis is correct (a think is a bus round-trip carrying the whole prompt, one trace stream per message, prompt blocks fetched by 0.25 s RPCs that silently vanish, assembly split between cognition/assembler.py and orchestration/context.py -- all verified) but the full package move is the riskiest diff for one developer. Resolution: take the harness's behavioural fixes first (single ContextBuilder with fixed prefix order; Kernel-injected in-process PersonaReader/SelfModelReader/MemoryReader in single mode, exactly as bus and ledger clients are injected, so the boundary test stays green) and the systems telemetry cut-over (which removes the per-message trace cost on its own); physically merge packages only after native tools and the session stream are in and gated.

LEDGER BACKEND AND TELEMETRY: systems switches the default to sqlite with spans/samples tables and row retention; harness keeps jsonl with batched fsync and trace streams per session; cognitive keeps fsync for action/task and batches high-volume streams; embodied is silent. Systems is right on the split: metrics:history (114 MB), curiosity:ticks (43 MB) and persona:state (17 MB) are paid at git-commit durability and the 88k trace streams are per message; the sqlite WAL backend already exists and is the documented local-multi engine. Harness's 'trace per session' is a half-measure. Decision streams (task, action, guardian, plan, memory writes) stay event-sourced on either backend; flipping their default to sqlite can wait for the eval gate.

GROWTH LAYER SHAPE: harness, cognitive and systems all merge learning+reflection+curiosity but disagree on the unit of learning -- harness: proposals through the harness scored by evals; cognitive: a versioned policy store with four artifact kinds and Thompson exploration; systems: skills only, competence from eval pass rates; embodied adds routine mining into HA automations. Cognitive's policy-artifact schema (id, kind, body, evidence_refs, evaluated_on, baseline, result, ttl, status) with eval-gated adoption, TTL and bounded rollback is the most complete and should be the container; systems' correction that competence must not come from self-reported chat outcomes is right (07 review item 11) -- feed posteriors from verify.result-backed outcomes and eval/benchmark results as separate weighted sources; harness's rule that the loop's only output type is a proposal through the gate is the safety property all three should share. Task-type rules first, skills second, code patches through the existing worktree landing; PatchPipeline deleted (verified unreachable).

BUS RPC vs IN-PROCESS FOR THE LOOP'S BRAIN. Harness collapses orchestration + cognition's assembler/parser/compaction into agent/ with Kernel-injected in-process Llm/MemoryReader/SelfModelReader/PersonaReader protocols; cognitive, systems and embodied keep cognition.think as a bus request. Harness has the better diagnosis (verified: context.py drops the memory block on a 0.25 s timeout as 'the normal case', the assembler drops persona/self on a 2 s timeout, the whole prompt rides the bus as a payload, and a 300 s handler timeout was once the wall budget). Resolution: one ContextBuilder inside orchestration (absorbing cognition/assembler.py's block order and context.py's memory block) with an explicit token budget per section, and a contracts-defined Llm protocol injected in single mode exactly as bus/ledger clients are, while the cognition.think topic stays for Planning, Memory consolidation and Verification. No file moves of providers/router/budget until the eval gate exists.

MEMORY REBUILD ORDER. All four agree on the target (embedder warmed in a boot thread, persisted vectors, BM25 + dense with rank fusion, facts with supersession, hashing as the floor). Harness schedules it at stage 7, cognitive at stage 2. Cognitive is right: it sits behind unchanged memory.retrieve/store contracts, does not depend on the tool protocol, and it is what the family feels daily (the falcon/sparrow and birthday cases are recorded in context.py). Supersession by data structure replaces the MEMORY_BLOCK_HEADER prose and flag_contradictions' symmetric 0.5 penalty.

Cognitive feeds the existing in-process WorkingMemory keyed by (person, channel); harness and systems put typed turns on a ledger session:<id>/thread stream; embodied keeps a per-(person, channel) conversation projection. Harness/systems are right for the destination: an in-process window dies on restart, which is exactly the observer's post-restart failure, and resume, replay, evals and compaction all need the same durable data. Cognitive's WorkingMemory wire is the correct one-week first increment and should not become the design.

UNIT OF SELF-IMPROVEMENT. All four merge learning + reflection + curiosity and delete the unreachable PatchPipeline (verified: learning/service.py reports UNREACHABLE; draft_candidate is not registered). Harness: skills first plus config/prompt PRs; systems: skills only, competence from evals; cognitive: four policy kinds with task-type rules rendered into scaffolds first; embodied: routines into HA. Systems/harness win: a skill is a file, diffable, Guardian-protectable and A/B-testable on the trial suite; a rule line injected into scaffolds is prompt self-modification whose 'only adds restrictions' promise cannot be checked mechanically, so it waits until per-task-type held-out sets exist and then lands as a committed file in the same protected directory as agent definitions. Cognitive's posteriors, Thompson sampling and compute_gaps wiring are grafted immediately regardless.

SAFETY POSTURE FOR PHYSICAL AND EXTERNAL EFFECTS. Systems (tiers 0-3, tier 3 human in every posture) and embodied (HomeRule/PersonRule/PresenceRule, separate physical posture) both restore the human gate; harness and cognitive leave the auto-approve default untouched. Systems/embodied are right and it is cheap: reversibility classes already exist on every tool, classify_call already exists as a pure function, and the exposure today is cam_siren and TV (HA unconfigured), so it must land before any HA token is configured. Systems' tier model is the general form; embodied's requester field is needed by both; harness's Guardian protection of agents/, hooks and the eval gate is the third piece and is compatible.

LEDGER COST AND TRACING. Systems: switch the decision log to sqlite and add spans/samples tables; harness and cognitive: per-turn appends, trace streams per session/task, batched fsync for telemetry, keep jsonl. Harness/cognitive first: the trace_id threading is half done (context.py already joins orchestration's requests to the task's stream; ~15 Cognition/Execution call sites remain), retention exists in ledger/compaction.py, and per-type sampling exists in bus/trace.py -- that removes most of the 88k trace streams without changing a backend. Systems' spans table is the right end state and the sqlite backend (verified: (stream, seq) PK, WAL, snapshots, blobs) makes it reachable, but a default-backend switch on a 1.4 GB live ledger is a migration with its own eval, not week 1.

STREAMING. Harness, systems and embodied all require provider streaming into Voice's existing StreamingSynthesiser/StreamingPlayer; cognitive omits it. The three are right: first audio is the family-felt latency (4-17 s full response), no provider streams today (verified), and it is independent of the tool protocol, so it belongs in the first quarter alongside native tools rather than after the growth merge.

INTERFACE. All agree dispatch.py (2,234 lines) must shrink and that the model should reach operator functions through schemas rather than the sim_command string tunnel; embodied's channels/admin package split and systems' by-domain split are moves that should wait until sessions are persistent and native tools exist, since both change the shape of what the TUI renders.

AGI FRAMING. No disagreement: all four say a harness around a frontier model does not become AGI by architecture, that generality is a measured coverage/horizon/continuity number in the ledger (blueprint 01 section 2.1 and section 3 already say this), and that the compounding investments are evals, the transcript/ledger, memory, skills and the safety chokepoint. The judge agrees; the only correction is that three of the four understate how much of the 'reasoning' program is simply choosing a stronger model tier per purpose, which is config today (routes['strong'] exists and is unset).
